Enjoy an expedition in comfort, luxury and safety whilst discovering the spectacular Antarctic environment. As well as watching the incredible wildlife (seals, whales, penguins and more), at certain times of year you can also dive, fish and climb.

The southern lights or Aurora Australis are visible in the night sky, diamond dust clouds can be seen under clear skies and sun dogs are an optical phenomenon viewed beside the sun. Embrace the magic of the Antarctic landscape from on board your own private yacht, on your terms.

destinations.name: East Greenland
destinations.summary: East Greenland offers a rare and untouched wilderness that’s perfect for exploring by yacht. With its pristine fjords, picturesque mountains and ice-carved landscapes, this remote part of the world is the ideal setting for an unforgettable charter experience.
destinations.metaTitle: Greenland Yacht Charter: Fjords, Ice and Arctic Wilderness
destinations.metaDescription: Charter an expedition yacht in East Greenland and cruise Scoresby Sund, the largest fjord system on earth, between July and September. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: East Greenland offers a rare and untouched wilderness that’s perfect for exploring by yacht. With its pristine fjords, picturesque mountains and ice-carved landscapes, this remote part of the world is the ideal setting for an unforgettable charter experience.
paragraphs: The tranquillity here is unmatched, enhanced by abundant wildlife and the sense of exclusivity that comes with such a secluded destination.

As the largest island on Earth, Greenland is renowned for its natural ice sculptures, snow-capped peaks, and awe-inspiring scenery. This unspoilt region is best experienced from the water, where the dramatic landscapes are brought to life.

With only 5% of Greenland’s population residing on the east coast, East Greenland offers unparalleled privacy. The isolation of this region means that the landscape remains unspoiled, and the air is incredibly clear—making it the perfect place to experience the Northern Lights. Sunrises and sunsets here are nothing short of breathtaking, especially when enjoyed from the water.

At the heart of East Greenland lies Scoresbysund, the largest fjord system in the world. This intricate network of fjords is roamed by local wildlife and it’s likely that you’ll catch a glimpse of some of Greenland’s iconic animals, including musk ox, seals, polar bears, and humpback whales. The undisturbed nature of this region makes it an extraordinary place for wildlife watching, providing a rare opportunity to witness these magnificent creatures in their natural habitat.

The settlement of Ittoqqortoormiit is one of the most remote communities in the world, home to multi-coloured houses making this area instantly recognisable. With a population of just 400, it offers a rare glimpse into what life is like in one of the world’s most secluded corners. For those looking to immerse themselves even further into the local culture, a guided tour by one of the friendly locals is available, providing a unique insight into the history and daily life of this Arctic community.

destinations.name: Svalbard
destinations.summary: Adored for its rugged landscapes, glistening glaciers and Arctic animals, Svalbard offers unparalleled scenery and plenty of opportunity for exploration.
destinations.metaTitle: Svalbard Yacht Charter: Arctic Glaciers and Polar Bears
destinations.metaDescription: Charter an expedition yacht in Svalbard and cruise glacier fronts, bird cliffs and polar bear country under the midnight sun. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: Adored for its rugged landscapes, glistening glaciers and Arctic animals, Svalbard offers unparalleled scenery and plenty of opportunity for exploration.
paragraphs: Its relaxed atmosphere and unspoilt views are just some of the things that make this archipelago popular amongst all who visit. Autumn and spring in Svalbard promise sweeping views of the Northern Lights, while the summer season offers midnight sun and still fjords nestled between towering mountains, making this area of Norway an incredible place to explore no matter the season.

Longyearbyen, located in the Westfjords, is a hub for land-based excursions and expeditions. Known for its rich history, the town is home to a number of unique museums where you’ll have the opportunity to dive into the stories of the region’s first explorers. During your stay, you can partake in guided snowmobile tours, venture into remote areas on a husky-drawn sled, or discover the intricate formations inside the ice caves.

For those seeking seclusion and natural beauty, the uninhabited island of Prins Karls Forland is a must-see. This pristine island is teeming with wildlife, including reindeer, Arctic foxes, walruses, and even polar bears. Its untouched landscapes offer an unparalleled sense of tranquillity, making it a rare and peaceful retreat within the Norwegian Fjords.

Isfjorden is another highlight, perfect for those wishing to immerse themselves in the area’s stunning natural surroundings. With a variety of scenic look out points and numerous hiking trails, this region offers panoramic views of the surrounding mountains, best experienced at sunrise.

destinations.summary: Cruise the iconic Great Barrier Reef and the Whitsunday Islands, where pristine waters and colourful reefs offer scuba diving and snorkelling among vibrant marine life. Experience Sydney from the water, explore its vibrant bays and cruise up the coast to Pittwater.
destinations.metaDescription: Australia is home to some of the best yacht charter destinations in the Southern Hemisphere, experience this incredible destination by way of yacht charter.
destinations.lede: You will find everything that dreams are made of on a superyacht charter in Australia, sailing under blue skies with a backdrop of awe-inspiring scenery.
paragraphs: Australia offers variety and diversity with thousands of miles of coastline to explore; coral reefs, historical ports, white beaches and so much more. Enjoy a unique experience at The Great Barrier Reef: this veritable utopia for underwater adventurers is home to some of the most exotic and rare marine creatures on the planet and ideal for exploring by superyacht. Throughout Australia, discover opportunities for fabulous water sports adventures, with endless possibilities for surfing, diving and fishing.

With its picture postcard views of the city, best savoured from the deck of a luxury superyacht, Sydney Harbour is probably one of the most stunning landscapes in the world. The city itself boasts a multitude of attractions, ranging from buzzing nightlife and excellent restaurants to widespread cultural opportunities.

Taking your Australian superyacht charter further along the coast, a visit to the famous Great Barrier Reef is essential. Home to some of the most exotic and rare marine creatures on the planet, discovering the hidden world beneath the crystal clear blue waters is an exceptional experience.

Trips inland are also recommended; Australia’s unique climatic zones and fascinating landscapes offer a melange of diverse entertainment and bewildering beauty. On the northern side, the continent is dominated by lush rainforests, with great opportunities to observe a range of fascinating, indigenous wildlife, flourishing in their natural habitat. Further to the south, deserts with far-reaching vistas dominate the landscape. Visit traditional Aborigine villages and explore first hand one of the most intriguing cultures on the planet.

destinations.name: The Leeward Islands
destinations.summary: Each of the stunning Leeward Islands offers something different, but what they all have in common is crystal clear azure waters and white sand beaches.
destinations.metaDescription: Explore our destination guide to a Leeward Islands yacht charter, the perfect sailing paradise for extended cruising for itineraries longer than one week.
paragraphs: Experience the essence of Caribbean beauty with a superyacht charter in the Leeward Islands. Spanning over 150 miles from Anguilla in the north to Dominica, the Leeward Islands offer a fascinatingly diverse selection of islands to explore. With excellent transport links and a well-developed yachting infrastructure, whether you seek a family adventure or an upscale celebration, the Leeward Islands are a perfect destination for a luxury yacht charter.

The Leeward Islands are a paradise for water sports enthusiasts, with excellent conditions for everything from windsurfing and kiteboarding to deep-sea fishing and scuba diving. The coral reefs are teeming with life, and there are numerous wrecks and dive sites to explore. If you’re looking for a more relaxed experience, you can simply drop anchor in a secluded bay and soak up the sun or swim in the crystal-clear Caribbean Sea.

When it comes to dining, the Leeward Islands offer an incredible range of options, from beachside shacks serving up local specialities to high-end restaurants helmed by Michelin-starred chefs. The local cuisine blends African, European, and Caribbean influences, with fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and spices taking centre stage. And if you’re in the mood for a party, the Leeward Islands are home to some of the liveliest nightlife in the Caribbean, with beach bars, clubs, and casinos.

The Leeward Islands offer outstanding natural beauty and are steeped in history, offering an inviting balance of Caribbean spirit and laidback luxury; where each island offers something unique to discover. Charter a luxury motor yacht or harness the power of mother nature aboard an elegant sailing boat and discover this paradisical destination in style.
Amongst the best Leeward Islands to drop anchor at are Antigua, Saba, St. Eustatius, St. Maarten, St. Thomas, Anguilla, Virgin Gorda, and St. Barts.

Spend a few days discovering the best of Antigua’s 365 beaches and sail into the famed English Harbour. The island’s unmistakable British ambience provides a window into a captivating and diverse history. One of the most significant historical landmarks is the UNESCO-protected Nelson’s Dockyard in English Harbour. As the oldest Georgian harbour still operational, it is the focal point for Antigua’s annual Sailing Week, a prominent event on the yachting calendar. The beaches are the island’s primary attractions, but its appeal also lies in its maritime history – combined, they have placed the island in pole position on the Caribbean map.

Our Leeward Islands yacht charter itinerary would be incomplete without mentioning the tiny island of Saba, which lies to the northwest. Saba boasts towering cliffs and volcanic peaks that rise out of the Caribbean Sea, creating a stunning coastline to cruise. While there are no beaches to speak of, diving and snorkelling are world-class. Hike into the island’s interior, and explore the lush rainforest teeming with life. Alternatively, explore the peaceful capital named The Bottom.

Nearby St. Eustatius, or “Statia” as it’s affectionately known, is an undiscovered gem. With its charming capital Oranjestad and fascinating yet poignant history that includes everything from pirates to the slave trade, chartering a yacht opens up precious opportunities to visit these lesser-known Caribbean treasures.

The bustling island of St. Maarten brings a distinctly cosmopolitan vibe, making it a must-visit on a Leeward Islands yacht charter. Divided into French and Dutch territories, St. Maarten’s Dutch side boasts a lively nightlife scene with casinos and nightclubs, while on the French side, gourmet cuisine and long, lazy days and French-influenced dinners are plentiful. The island’s cultural mix matches its diverse scenery, with European-style cafes and chic boutiques lining whitewashed Caribbean beaches. The adventurous can even follow a crew-led mission to the 424m-high Paradise Peak or fly above a mango plantation on an extreme zip line.

As you step ashore at St. Thomas, you’ll be welcomed by the sights and sounds of one of the Caribbean’s most vibrant and sophisticated islands. A lively party atmosphere is guaranteed with an array of bars, clubs, and restaurants catering to every taste and mood. And for those who love to indulge in a little retail therapy, the island’s tax-free shopping is an absolute must.

St. Thomas is not just about partying and shopping. Indeed, the island boasts a rich and fascinating history, dating back to the days of pirates and colonial sugar plantations. There are plenty of opportunities to explore the island’s past, with historical sites and museums that offer a glimpse into St. Thomas’s intriguing past.

Anguilla, a British Overseas Territory, is also worth discovering during your Leeward Islands yacht charter. The island’s natural beauty, including some of the best beaches in the world, has been preserved while still offering luxurious retreats and a range of activities for superyacht charter guests to enjoy.

Sailing along the island’s idyllic coastline, one can enjoy the crystal-clear waters and spot the native red-billed tropicbirds. Anguilla’s rich wildlife and impressive wrecks and coral reefs below the waves, provide endless options for activities for yacht enthusiasts. Join local islanders and dance to live reggae on the powdered sugar sands of Shoal Bay or participate in one of Anguilla’s regular regattas.

Beyond the beaches, Anguilla offers rugged landscapes to explore, and golf enthusiasts will appreciate Anguilla’s golf course designed by golf legend Greg Norman. Take a day trip to Prickly Pear Cays, a truly secluded island just off Anguilla’s western coast, or visit the protected areas of Big Spring Cave, known for its prehistoric petroglyphs, or East End Pond, a wildlife conservation site.

With its unspoiled innocence and laid-back atmosphere, Anguilla is a destination that exudes the casual, low-key elegance that discerning travellers seek. Whether you’re sipping a rum punch while gazing out at the famous Shoal Bay sunset or enjoying the island’s many other charms, Anguilla is a place that will captivate your senses. And now, with a superyacht marina in development, Anguilla is quickly becoming a favourite among the yachting crowd.

Anguilla isn’t alone as a destination that appeals to those seeking sun-soaked adventure and tranquil escapes. The next recommendation on our Leeward Islands yacht charter itinerary is nestled among the British Virgin Islands. Virgin Gorda is a superyacht charter destination that beckons with its plethora of scenic beaches, stunning coral reefs, and world-renowned resorts. For those who wish to explore the Caribbean in style and luxury, Virgin Gorda is an excellent choice. Whether you want to indulge in the ultimate relaxation or seek out thrilling watersports, this island paradise has it all.

Virgin Gorda’s scenic charm extends beyond its stunning coral sand beaches though. The island’s interior is dotted with hidden treasures, such as the ruins of the Spanish fortress at the Little Fort National Park and the National Parks at Devil’s Bay, North Sound, Spring Bay and Gorda Peak. The island is also home to one of the world’s top 10 wreck dive sites – the RMS Rhone – a must-visit for avid divers.

St. Barts, the ‘it’ island with red-tiled roofs, French cuisine, and high-end boutiques, offers the most luxurious experience of all the isles. With every amenity expected of exclusive resorts, including excellent restaurants and designer boutiques, this unique and sophisticated island exudes a South-of-France feel with a tropical backdrop.

A short cruise south, berth in the fully serviced Christophe Harbour in St. Kitts. Perfectly positioned to the south of the island for access to the capital Basse Terre and an abundance of historical sites. Step ashore and discover rolling sugarcane fields, plantation ruins, and merchant houses now home to boutique hotel properties for a fascinating insight into this stunning island’s colonial past.

A Leeward Islands yacht charter is an unforgettable experience, offering a unique blend of luxury and adventure in one of the world’s most beautiful destinations. Whether you’re seeking relaxation, adventure, or a little bit of both, the Leeward Islands truly have it all.

destinations.lede: The Virgin Islands, a collection of over 100 islands and cays, are divided into two main territories: the British Virgin Islands (BVI) and the U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI).
paragraphs: With year-round warm temperatures averaging 25-30°C (77-86°F), this tropical destination is perfect for yachting, though the prime season runs from December to April, when the trade winds make for ideal sailing conditions. Each region offers a distinct experience, from the bustling harbours of St. Thomas in the USVI to the secluded coves of Tortola in the BVIs.

For superyacht charters, the Virgin Islands offer an unmatched blend of natural beauty and exclusivity. Itineraries might include snorkelling or diving in gin-clear waters teeming with marine life around the famous Baths of Virgin Gorda or the underwater national parks of St. John. Guests can enjoy glorious isolation at uninhabited islands and quiet gems like Anegada, famous for its coral reefs and flamingos, or sip a cocktail at one of the chic beach bars on Jost Van Dyke.

Always a hit for families with young children, the Virgin Islands are renowned for their rich biodiversity, where you can spot sea turtles, stingrays, and dolphins everyday. Sailing between islands is a breeze, with each new stop offering something unique—whether it’s a private beach picnic, world-class watersports, or simply soaking in the incredible Caribbean sunsets. For both relaxation and adventure, the Virgin Islands always deliver.

destinations.name: Belize
destinations.summary: Hosting the second largest barrier reef in the world, a host of multi-cultural delights and over 200 beautiful sandy isles, Belize is a stunning yacht charter destination.
destinations.metaDescription: Home to over 200 beautiful sandy isles and the second largest barrier reef in the world: Belize is a magical yacht charter destination.
destinations.lede: Hosting the second largest barrier reef in the world, a host of multi-cultural delights and over 200 beautiful sandy isles, Belize is a stunning yacht charter destination. Discover Mayan ruins, diverse wildlife and superb diving along the jungle-lined coast.
paragraphs: A former British colony, Belize’s national language is English, spoken with a Caribbean lilt. Packed full of cays, coves and coral, the coastal areas are a divers' paradise just waiting to be explored. Inland, Mayan history is featured in numerous archaeological temples and palaces. To get a fully immersive experience, hike the Maya Mountains - covered with lush sub-tropical forests and home to a vast selection of wildlife, the many trails are also strewn with captivating ancient ruins.

Diving and snorkelling are wildly popular in Belize. The massive barrier reef offers unlimited opportunities to explore the underwater world up close. To the north, Cayes Ambergris, Caulker and Half Moon are highly recommended destinations, along with Turneffe Reef Atoll. The quieter south is highly focused on marine conservation, notably in the Sapodilla Cayes Marine Path, which is on the migratory path for whale sharks. For a digital detox, sea kayaking in the region is the perfect way to skip from cay to cove and indulge in some peaceful fishing. Centrally located in Belize, St Herman's Blue Hole National Park is famed for turquoise waters scattered with ancient Mayan artefacts. This is not to be confused with the world-renowned Great Blue Hole, a giant marine sinkhole off the country’s coast.

destinations.name: Costa Rica
destinations.summary: The small central American country of Costa Rica is tucked between the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. The secluded coastline is bursting with natural beauty and stunning beaches.
destinations.metaDescription: Costa Rica yacht charter offers dense jungles, volcanos and white water rafting. The perfect charter destination for both relaxation and adventure.
paragraphs: The small central American country of Costa Rica is tucked between the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. The secluded coastline is bursting with natural beauty and stunning beaches.

As one of the most biodiverse counties in the world, Costa Rica is an extraordinary destination for a yacht charter. Discover tropical forests, towering volcanoes, exciting wildlife and a wonderful culture.

Found on the Caribbean coast, the Tortuguero National Park, has been labelled a “little Amazon.” Home to exotic wildlife and indigenous plants, visitors can explore on foot or adventurers may prefer to take a thrilling zip-line ride across the rainforest canopy.

Known for its natural wonders, the national park at Cocos Island is a World Heritage Site on the Pacific side. Once a hideout for pirates, you can spot dolphins, hammerhead sharks, humpback whales and turtles in its coastal waters.
Famed for its “Pura Vida”, meaning “pure life”, Costa Rica is a destination not to be missed.

destinations.summary: Mexico awaits yachting enthusiasts with its stunning landscapes, fine weather and unique cuisine; paired with a friendly population.
destinations.metaDescription: Mexico awaits yacht charter enthusiasts with its stunning landscapes, fine weather and unique cuisine, from the Baja Peninsula to the Mayan Riviera.
destinations.lede: Famous for its stunning shorelines, fine weather and delicious food, Mexico is a great choice for yachting enthusiasts.
paragraphs: West Mexico has its very own magic. From Baja California down to Oaxaca, you will find some of the most fascinating spots in the Pacific providing an excellent cruising ground for yachts.

To the east, the Yucatan Peninsula is proud of its Mayan ancestry. In Quintana Roo you can find fascinating archaeological sites mingled with fine bars and restaurants along 120 miles of scenic coastline. The most famous and coveted stop-over, especially by yacht, is with no doubt Cancun. Located at the edge of Quintana Roo, it is on the Yucatan Channel that separates Mexico from Cuba.

The town of Acapulco, nestled in a natural horseshoe-shaped bay, is one of the main attractions on the western coast of Mexico and is ideal for those who wish to indulge in urban life. The hills and cliffs around the bay are sprinkled with restaurants and bars, all providing fantastic views of Acapulco and the ocean below.

destinations.name: The Maldives
destinations.summary: Located in the heart of the Indian Ocean, the Maldives is a dream destination for those searching for pristine waters and exceptional diving. Discover coral atolls, remote sandbanks and some of the world’s richest vibrant marine life, making every luxury yacht charter here truly unforgettable.
destinations.metaDescription: Over 1,200 islands to explore, thriving marine life and golden beaches; the Maldives is an Indian Ocean yacht charter paradise.
destinations.lede: Home to some of the most consistently perfect beaches in the world, where over 1,000 islands are fringed by white powdery sand and lapped by luminous azure waters – the Maldives is paradise personified.
paragraphs: The 26 ring-shaped atolls of the Maldives provide the perfect diving and snorkeling environment, with the crystal-clear water acting as a magnet to those keen to experience life below the waves. Adding to the appeal, the water is so warm there is rarely a need for a wetsuit. Discover glorious caves, dazzling coral walls and schools of brightly coloured tropical fish, with the deeper waters being home to a range of manta rays, turtles and reef sharks.
Several atolls offer ideal conditions for board and kite surfing and are also renown for big-game fishing. For something more low-key, visit the fishermen islands and absorb the Maldivian culture.

destinations.name: Seychelles
destinations.summary: Strewn with World Heritage Sites, the granite archipelago of the Seychelles clusters together over 100 mostly uninhabited islands, dotted with picturesque hidden bays and awe-inspiring scenery.
destinations.metaDescription: Strewn with World Heritage Sites, the granite archipelago of the Seychelles is a stunning yacht charter destination for snorkelling and relaxing alike.
destinations.lede: Strewn with World Heritage Sites, the granite archipelago of the Seychelles clusters together over 100 mostly uninhabited islands, dotted with picturesque hidden bays and awe-inspiring scenery.
paragraphs: Located in the north east of Madagascar, the Seychelles island group is a popular superyacht charter destination with the lure of exceptional underwater pursuits and captivating landscapes. Due to its exceptional beauty, Praslin Island is considered the original site of the mythical Garden of Eden and is certainly worth a visit.

Amongst the oldest islands in the world, this barefoot getaway is swathed in miles of untouched shores, sprinkled with tropical flowers and inhabited by rare wildlife. When chartering a superyacht in the Seychelles, be sure to make time for a private picnic lunch on a ribbon of powdery sand flanked by crystalline waters and granite boulders, where you might be joined by the odd sea turtle.

Synonymous with the Seychelles is of course its beaches; top picks include the famous Anse Source d’Argent, out-of-the-way Anse Marron and pretty Anse Lazio. Escape to the remote bliss of Denis Private Island or be transported back in time to serene La Digue, where cars are strictly prohibited. Anchor at the Aldabra Atoll, an awe-inspiring, protected island group surrounded by coral reefs with excellent snorkelling and also home to giant tortoises, manta rays and tiger sharks.

If you are looking for chic sophistication, go to Intendence Bay for luxurious surroundings and exquisite restaurants. Alternatively, those seeking adventure should head inland for incredible mountain walks, cascading waterfalls and rock climbing activities.
From emerald jungles to secret anchorages, idyllic beaches to dramatic shipwrecks, the Seychelles delivers an enchanting superyacht charter destination you will long to return to again and again.

destinations.name: Tanzania
destinations.summary: Enjoy a hushed balloon flight over the Serengeti savannah plains, experience a big game safari or swim with Whale Sharks – just some of the things you can do in the extraordinary country of Tanzania.
destinations.metaDescription: Tanzania offers a heady mix of nature, culture and scenery guarantees to excite and mesmerize makes for a memorable luxury yacht charter.
destinations.lede: Enjoy a hushed balloon flight over the Serengeti savannah plains, experience a big game safari or swim with whale sharks – just some of the things you can do in the extraordinary country that is Tanazania.
paragraphs: Home to the Serengeti National Park, Africa’s highest mountain and the exceptional cruising grounds of the Spice Islands – Tanzania offers a yachting experience with a difference.

You can be assured of a warm welcome in this eminent land of safaris, Swahili locals and Maasia warriors. Watch ungainly hippos jostle for space in muddy pools, sagacious elephants amble well-trodden paths and headstrong wildebeest run across the plains. Organised boat safaris down the Rufijji River observe somnolent crocodiles at the Selous Game Reserve and at Ruaha National Park spot graceful giraffes amidst aged baobab trees.

Quiet littoral villages dot the Indian Ocean coastline, whilst remotely serene islands create bygone scenes as wooden dhows with flowing sails glide by on the warm breeze. For exceptional diving and snorkelling, be sure to visit the relatively isolated Island of Pemba with its diverse sea life and vivid coral.
With its flamboyant culture, outstanding dive site and historical UNESCO cities, Tanzania offers a yacht charter experience like no where else.

destinations.name: Croatia
destinations.summary: Croatia’s Adriatic coastline is home to medieval towns, secluded bays and more than a thousand islands waiting to be explored. Historic cities such as Dubrovnik and Split offer a vibrant cultural mix alongside beautiful coastlines and calm waters ideal for a luxury yacht charter.
destinations.metaTitle: Croatia Yacht Charter: Dubrovnik, Hvar & the Adriatic | OI
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a luxury yacht in Croatia and sail the stunning Adriatic coastline. Explore Dubrovnik, Hvar, Korcula, and the Dalmatian islands with OI.
paragraphs: Renowned for its natural beauty, Croatia is a highly favoured summer yacht charter destination, where pretty harbours and sun-blushed islands lure superyachts across the Adriatic.

Unspoiled and brimming with history, where old and new are seamlessly woven together, a Croatia yacht charter will take you on a journey to some of the most spectacular venetian towns and secluded bays, appreciated best from the water. This is the Mediterranean as it was always meant to be.

With more than a thousand islands, explore one of the most beautiful coastlines in Europe, Croatia's Dalmatian coast. Breath-taking views of soaring mountains, cascading waterfalls, and ancient olive trees dotting gently rolling hills have captivated many famous writers. From Lord Byron and Dante, to Agatha Christie and George Bernard Shaw who aptly described Dubrovnik as 'heaven on earth,' Croatia has long attracted visitors from all over the world.

With more than 1,000 islands and roughly 1,700 miles of coastline, Croatia is one of the Mediterranean’s most rewarding yacht charter destinations, and our charter experts place clients across the Adriatic coast every season.

From the southern Dalmatian islands to historic harbour towns and quiet anchorages, a Croatia yacht charter vacation combines crystal clear seas, exceptional island hopping and coastline stretching from Istria to Dubrovnik.

Whether clients wish to sail Croatia aboard a luxury motor yacht, a sailing yacht or a fully crewed superyacht, our fleet delivers access to medieval cities, sandy beaches, national parks and secluded bays that are difficult to reach any other way. The combination of reliable summer sailing conditions, modern marinas and traditional Croatian culture continues to make Croatia one of the most requested destinations in our Mediterranean portfolio.

Croatia’s position between Central Europe and the Mediterranean has created a rich blend of Croatian culture, traditional Croatian cuisine, medieval cities and ancient towns that remain central to the charter experience today. From Roman remains and Venetian architecture to waterfront promenades and family-run konobas, each stop along the Adriatic coast offers a distinct sense of place.
Dubrovnik, often referred to as the “Pearl of the Adriatic”, is a UNESCO World Heritage site celebrated for its preserved medieval architecture and fortified old town overlooking the Adriatic coast.

Croatia offers one of the Mediterranean’s most varied charter grounds, combining short cruising distances with exceptional sailing conditions, historic coastal towns and over a thousand islands to explore.

Croatia offers a range of yacht charter formats to suit different levels of sailing experience and onboard service expectations, from hands-on bareboat charters to fully crewed superyacht experiences along the Adriatic coast.

Bareboat charters suit experienced sailors who want to sail Croatia independently. Clients are responsible for navigation, mooring and route planning throughout the charter. Croatian regulations require a valid sailing licence and VHF radio licence onboard, and single-handed sailing is prohibited, meaning at least two people must be on board at all times.

A skippered yacht charter combines independence with local expertise. Clients can still take the helm while a professional skipper manages routing, harbour approaches, weather conditions and mooring logistics. This option is ideal for experienced sailors seeking a lighter operational load along the Adriatic coast.

Fully crewed charter yachts represent the majority of our Croatia fleet. A Captain, chef and interior crew manage every aspect of the experience, from itinerary planning to onboard service. Weekly charter fees for luxury motor yachts typically begin at around EUR 25,000 and can exceed EUR 350,000 for larger superyachts. Motor yachts remain the most popular option in Croatia, while sailing yachts, catamarans and traditional gulets offer alternative cruising styles for families and longer island-hopping itineraries.

Indulge in a truly exceptional culinary experience at Restaurant 360°, perched atop the majestic city walls of Dubrovnik. Here, the breathtaking panorama of the ancient city and the shimmering harbour below serves as a stunning backdrop to the gastronomic marvels created by Chef Marijo Curi – the mastermind behind this Michelin-starred restaurant.

Famed for his innovative use of modern techniques and locally-sourced Croatian ingredients, Chef Curi has created a degustation menu that is truly unparalleled in its artistry and taste. Each dish is a sensory delight, carefully crafted to showcase the very best of Croatian cuisine. And, to complement this culinary extravaganza, the restaurant’s extensive wine cellar features an impeccable selection of world-class wines, each one thoughtfully chosen to enhance the flavours of the dishes on offer.

Nestled on the idyllic island of Ist lies the charming town of Rovinj, a treasure trove of culinary delights. Here, Monte, the first Croatian restaurant to be bestowed with the coveted Michelin star, awaits discerning travellers seeking an unforgettable dining experience. With an unwavering commitment to culinary excellence, Chef Danijel Eki’s artistry shines through in each dish, skillfully crafted using the freshest, locally sourced ingredients that showcase the essence of Istria’s rich culinary heritage.

From the succulent flavours of fresh seafood to the fragrant notes of locally produced white truffle oil and extra virgin olive oil, the ever-changing menu at Monte is a testament to Chef Eki’s culinary prowess. If you’re planning a luxurious yacht charter in Croatia, a visit to Monte is an absolute must, promising an unparalleled gastronomic journey that will linger on your taste buds long after your voyage has ended.

Perched high above the breathtaking St. James Cathedral, Pelegrini stands tall as yet another culinary crown jewel in the land of Croatia. With Chef Rudi Stefan’s innovative approach to Dalmatian cuisine, the restaurant effortlessly transforms traditional dishes into modern-day masterpieces, showcasing the finest local seafood and produce.

For those traversing the central Dalmatian coast by superyacht, Pelegrini is an essential stop. Its elegant terrace provides a stunning setting for a romantic evening, while the menu leaves an indelible mark on the palate. A visit to this gastronomical haven is an experience to be savoured, and one that will be fondly remembered for years to come.

An evening of culinary splendour awaits at Zagreb’s acclaimed Noel. Though it may be tempting to linger on the breathtaking Croatian coastline, a visit to this Michelin-starred gem is well worth the slight detour.

Chef Goran Koi’s contemporary European menu boasts a Croatian twist, featuring only the freshest seasonal ingredients from the region. Each dish is crafted with meticulous attention to detail, delivering a culinary journey that is both refined and imaginative. Pair your meal with a selection from their extensive wine list, which includes both domestic and foreign labels, ensuring the perfect complement to your dining experience. For those seeking the ultimate in luxurious gastronomic indulgence, a visit to Noel is simply a must.

Despite its informal ambiance, Bokeria Kitchen & Wine Bar delivers an unmistakably Mediterranean dining experience. The cosy setting, reminiscent of the legendary La Boqueria Market in Barcelona, adds to the restaurant’s charm and allure.

At Bokeria, the attentive and knowledgeable staff will guide you through their extensive wine list, helping you to select the perfect pairing for your meal. After an exhilarating day of sailing around the captivating Croatian islands on a luxurious yacht charter, a leisurely dinner at Bokeria by the marina in Split is the ideal way to unwind and savour the flavours of Croatia. Embark on a culinary adventure at Bokeria Kitchen & Wine Bar, where every bite is an experience to cherish.
The official sailing season in Croatia runs from April to October, with conditions varying throughout the summer season.

Most charters in Croatia operate on weekly charter blocks, typically beginning and ending on Saturdays. Our charter experts manage all financial and operational details in advance, ensuring clients have complete transparency before embarkation.
Weekly rates for smaller crewed motor yachts generally begin at around EUR 25,000, while the largest luxury motor yachts and superyachts can exceed EUR 350,000 per week.

Usually 25 to 40% of the charter fee and paid in advance to cover fuel, food, beverages, dockage, communications and client preferences throughout the charter. Remaining funds are reconciled at the end of the trip.
A 13% VAT rate applies to charters commencing and remaining within Croatian waters. This is calculated on the base charter fee and paid alongside the APA.
Depending on season and location, marina and town quay mooring fees generally range from EUR 50 to EUR 250+ per night.
Our Team advises clients on suitable yachts, preferred cruising regions and expected operational costs before confirming the charter.
Croatia’s coastline offers everything from secluded coves and pebble shores to sandy beaches accessible only by charter yacht.

A jewel in the crown of Croatia’s breathtaking coastline, Zlatni Rat, so-called for its distinctive shape, is one of the most well-known beaches in all of Croatia. This pristine pebble beach on the island of Brač offers stunning panoramic views of the crystalline blue Adriatic Sea.

Adventurers seeking an adrenaline rush will find no shortage of thrilling activities here. From windsurfing to jet skiing, Zlatni Rat is a playground for water sports enthusiasts. And what better way to indulge in these aquatic pursuits than on a luxurious Croatia yacht charter?

As the day winds down and the sun begins to set, head to the charming town of Bol for a dose of excitement. With its vibrant nightlife and lively atmosphere, Bol is the perfect destination for those seeking a little adventure after a day of sightseeing.

On the southeastern coast of Vis Island lies a hidden gem that is every traveller’s dream – Stiniva Beach. This secret cove boasts an air of exclusivity and tranquillity, making it the ultimate destination for yacht charters seeking seclusion and privacy.

Magnificent limestone cliffs encompass the area creating a breathtaking backdrop that perfectly complements the crystal-clear waters of the Adriatic Sea. And what better way to bask in this exquisite setting than dropping anchor and soaking up the beauty of your surroundings from the privacy of a luxury yacht?

Adding to the draw of Stiniva Beach is its charming pebble beach, which boasts glistening waters that beckon you to take a dip. And for those who seek respite from the sun’s rays, a quaint beach bar is on hand to provide refreshment and relaxation ashore.

Nestled just beyond Dubrovnik’s iconic city walls lies a veritable oasis for the discerning traveller – Banje Beach. A true gem of the Adriatic, this pristine stretch of sand beckons to those lucky enough to be embarking on a yacht charter in Croatia. With its vivacious ambiance and unparalleled vistas of both the Old Town and the idyllic island of Lokrum, Banje Beach simply must be experienced firsthand.

After basking in the sun and soaking up the unparalleled views, indulge in a feast for the senses at the Banje Beach Club. Savour delectable cuisine and sip on refreshing cocktails, all while being pampered like a VIP. For the ultimate in luxury, look no further than Banje Beach – a place where relaxation and sophistication merge seamlessly.

Indulge in the pinnacle of luxury and immerse yourself in the unbridled beauty of Lubenice Beach on Cres Island. A destination so exclusive, it can only be accessed by boat or via a challenging hike. This sanctuary where time stands still, and peace and quiet reign supreme, Lubenice Beach is a haven for the discerning traveller yearning for a respite from the hustle and bustle of the modern world.

The immaculate waters that lap the shores of Lubenice Beach are ideal for snorkelling and swimming, allowing you to immerse yourself in the underwater world teeming with life. Get lost in the moment and allow the natural beauty to wash over you, enveloping you in a sense of profound contentment.

Sakarun Beach is a coveted destination amongst discerning travellers, lured by its serene and unassuming bohemian charm. Nestled within the expanse of Dugi Otok, one of the Zadar archipelago’s greatest and least populated islands, Sakarun Beach on Croatia’s renowned coastline is a sight to behold.

After indulging in the opulence of a day spent basking under the balmy Croatian sun onboard your private luxury yacht, retire to the beach’s quaint bar and relish in the picturesque spectacle of the sun dipping below the horizon, with a refreshing beverage in hand.
Croatia’s marinas combine modern superyacht facilities with traditional town quays and quiet bays that suit a wide range of charter itineraries across the Adriatic coast.

Nestled in the heart of the enchanting city of Split, lies a true gem of the Adriatic – the ACI Marina Split. Imbued with a sense of timeless elegance and sophistication, this marina beckons to the discerning traveller seeking an unrivalled yachting experience in Croatia.
With 318 immaculately maintained berths and the ability to accommodate superyachts up to 90 metres, this is the ideal haven for the discerning traveller seeking to explore the Adriatic in style.

Unwind and immerse yourself in the captivating culture and cuisine of Split. Diocletian’s Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the city centre are a mere stroll away, inviting you to discover the rich history and vibrant energy of this enchanting city.

As the perfect starting point to a journey of unparalleled exploration in Croatia, ACI Marina Split offers a launching point to explore the pristine waters of the Adriatic, discover hidden coves, and immerse yourself in the natural beauty of this idyllic destination.

Marina Frapa beckons the charter connoisseur seeking a haven of luxury and refinement. With an impressive array of 462 berths catering to yachts up to 54 metres in length, Marina Frapa, located in the centre of Rogoznica, stands as an impeccable testament to nautical sophistication.

With multiple awards for its unparalleled facilities and exceptional customer service, indulge in a truly memorable stay both on and off your superyacht. With Marina Frapa’s opulent five-star hotel, sparkling swimming pools, exquisite restaurants, and buzzing nightclub.

For those seeking adventure and exploration, the breathtaking Kornati National Park and the ancient city of Šibenik are conveniently located just a short drive away. Discover the rich history and culture of this magnificent region, with its picturesque villages, quaint towns, and vibrant nightlife.

A city steeped in history and culture, Dubrovnik simply cannot be missed on your Croatia yacht charter. Beneath this captivating city lies the ACI Marina Dubrovnik – a luxurious marina that offers unrivalled comfort and convenience. Boasting an impressive 380 berths, this yacht sanctuary caters to vessels up to 60 metres in length, providing an exceptional experience for superyacht Owners and charter guests alike.

Located a mere 6 kilometres from the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Dubrovnik’s Old Town, the ACI Marina Dubrovnik serves as the ideal starting point for exploring Croatia’s enchanting coast. Be sure to indulge in the spectacular views from the Dubrovnik Cable Car, or wander the ancient city walls and soak in the mesmerising scenery. As the day draws to a close, retreat to your superyacht berthed in this world-class harbour, where you can revel in the ultimate luxury and comfort that only a superyacht can provide.

Close to the charming town of Sukosan lies the coveted D-Marin Dalmacija, an enchanting marina that embodies the very essence of luxurious living. As the largest marina in Croatia, it offers a captivating stopover for superyachts of up to 80 metres in length. With a staggering 1,200 berths, this nautical haven is renowned for its impeccable service and steadfast dedication to environmental sustainability.

Savour the alluring beauty of the Kornati Islands, situated just a stone’s throw from this illustrious marina and immerse yourself in their staggering natural beauty. Discover the historic city of Zadar, where the sunsets are nothing short of spectacular and the calming melodies of the Sea Organ are sure to lull you into a state of blissful tranquillity. Experience the pinnacle of opulence at D-Marin Dalmacija, where memories are made and the possibilities are endless.

Nestled in the heart of the ancient city of Šibenik, lies the exquisite D-Marin Mandalina. This exclusive private marina boasts an impressive 429 slips and can accommodate superyachts up to 140 metres in length, making it the ultimate retreat for those on some of the worlds largest yachts seeking absolute seclusion.

Beyond its impressive mooring facilities, D-Marin Mandalina offers an unparalleled level of luxury and comfort, with lavish amenities including a state-of-the-art spa, fully equipped gym, and a variety of fine dining establishments serving the most delectable of cuisine.

For those with a passion for nature and culture, the marina’s prime location provides easy access to the breathtaking Krka National Park and the magnificent St. James Cathedral, both UNESCO-protected treasures that are a true feast for the senses.

On your luxury Croatia yacht charter be sure to head to the island of Korčula, known as “Little Dubrovnik ” for its beautiful mediaeval town. Within the honey-coloured walls that enclose Korčula Town, you’ll find a labyrinth of winding streets and stunning venetian-style architecture. Korčula is widely recognised as the birthplace of Marco Polo and remains one of Croatia’s best-preserved medieval island towns. And if you happen to be in Korčula at the right time, do not miss the riveting Moreska Sword Dance, an exhilarating local tradition.

Pula – a city steeped in history that dates back over three millennia. Here lies one of the largest and most complete Roman amphitheatres in the world, a testament to the enduring legacy of this ancient civilization. Witness the incredible preservation of this once-blood-soaked arena, which now serves as a majestic stage for dazzling cultural performances ranging from music to film.

But the wonders of Pula do not end there. Take in the other awe-inspiring Roman monuments scattered throughout the city, such as the iconic Arch of the Sergii and the majestic Temple of Augustus. With each step, you’ll find a reminder of the incredible feats of human ingenuity that have shaped our world.

Hvar is considered one of the ten most beautiful islands in the world, combining ancient towns, lively waterfronts and crystal-clear waters along the southern Dalmatian coast. This idyllic island boasts breathtaking landscapes, from fragrant lavender fields to crystal-clear waters, it is a true paradise on Earth.

As you drop anchor in Hvar’s picturesque harbour, take a moment to admire the stunning Cathedral of St. Stephen and the charming piazza that surrounds it. And, to truly indulge in the opulence of this island, treat yourself to a sumptuous five-star meal at one of Hvar’s many gourmet restaurants before embarking on a night out at one of the chic bars or clubs that line the island’s lavish waterfront. Hvar is truly a must-see for any discerning traveller seeking the pinnacle of luxury and relaxation.

Embark on a journey to the enchanting island of Vis, tucked away in the midst of the Dalmatian region, and indulge in a truly authentic and off-the-beaten-path experience. As the most remote inhabited island from the Croatian coast, Vis exudes a serene and unspoiled charm that is sure to captivate even the most discerning traveller.

Immerse yourself in the rich cultural heritage of the Dalmatian region, as you explore the island’s storied history and mingle with the friendly locals. A visit to the famed Blue Cave is a must, where the interplay of sunlight and seawater casts a mesmerising blue glow that is truly breathtaking.
A journey along the stunning coastline of Croatia aboard a luxurious yacht charter is an experience unlike any other, and no itinerary is complete without a visit to the ancient city of Dubrovnik.

Allow yourself to be swept away on a journey of discovery through the labyrinthine limestone-paved streets, taking in the impressive grandeur of the Rector’s Palace and its surrounding buildings. For a truly breathtaking experience, climb the stairs up to the iconic city walls and marvel at the panoramic vistas of the glittering Adriatic that stretch out before you.

To complete your indulgent Dubrovnik adventure, retreat to a boutique hotel that exudes a sense of elegance and exclusivity. Here, you will be enveloped in the city’s elite culture and receive an unparalleled level of personalised service that caters to your every whim.

Split, a flawless embodiment of timeless beauty and modernity. On your Croatia yacht charter delve into its rich past, where the ancient history effortlessly blends with contemporary city life, showcasing a harmonious coexistence like no other.

Diocletian’s Palace, an architectural masterpiece situated in the very heart of the city, stands as a testament to the city’s remarkable heritage, and has been deemed a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Here, Roman ruins stand as a proud testament to the city’s past, while lively marketplaces and cosy cafés buzz with the effervescence of the present.

And if you’re in the mood for some fresh air and breathtaking views of the city and harbour, take a stroll through the nearby Marjan Park. A lush green oasis, it offers a serene escape from the hustle and bustle of city life.

Amidst the stunning landscape of Mljet Island, the magnificent Mljet National Park beckons the nature lovers. With its breathtaking turquoise saltwater lakes,verdant forests, and diverse wildlife, this park is a veritable paradise for those seeking a truly immersive experience in the lap of nature.

Embark on an unforgettable adventure and anchor in one of the park’s secluded coves and step ashore to explore the national park at your leisure. Take a gentle walk and revel in the tranquillity of this unspoiled paradise. Or immerse yourself in the cool and refreshing waters of the park’s mesmerising lakes, and marvel at the rich marine life that thrives in the crystal-clear waters that embrace this island gem.

The picturesque Old Town of Dubrovnik serves as the backdrop for the annual Dubrovnik Summer Festival, a celebration of music, theatre, and dance. The 45-day festival features performances by both established and emerging artists from around the world in unusual settings like castles, plazas, and gardens. If you charter a yacht and drop anchor in the harbour, you can easily explore the city’s lively festival.

Every year, the picturesque city of Split plays host to the world-famous Split International Film Festival, a showcase for indie filmmakers. Short films, features, and experimental works from all over the world will be screened during this week-long celebration of cinema. Split is a great port of call for yacht charters in Croatia thanks to its lively waterfront and beautiful Diocletian’s Palace.

The annual Rovinj Wine Festival is not to be missed by any true wine aficionados. Over a hundred vintners from the region are expected to attend this two-day celebration of the best Istrian wines. In addition to tasting world-class vintages, you can chat with the winemakers behind them and pick their brains about the special Istrian soil and climate that contribute to their creations. You can enjoy the beautiful scenery of Rovinj’s Old Town from the deck of your superyacht, which you can dock at the nearby marina.

The Outlook & Dimensions Festival is the place to be if you enjoy electronic music. These two concerts, held back-to-back in Pula’s historic Fort Punta Christo, will blow your mind with their blend of innovative sound and breathtaking scenery. Listen to top-tier DJs and watch live performances until the wee hours of the morning, then unwind in the luxury of your superyacht.

The Vis Regatta is a thrilling annual sailing competition that departs from Split and concludes on the picturesque island of Vis. Sailors from all over the world, representing a wide variety of yacht classes, compete in this exciting race. From the comfort of your own superyacht, you can watch the Vis Regatta, renowned for its fierce competition and friendly atmosphere, and cheer on your favourite team.

Hvar is the perfect place to begin your exploration of the vibrant nightlife of Croatia. Carpe Diem is a famous, upmarket beach club and lounge bar that becomes a lively party spot after dark. This exclusive hangout is a favourite of celebrities and jetsetters, making it a great choice for your Croatia yacht charter. Take advantage of the resort’s private beach during the day, and then hit the dance floor to the sounds of international DJs as the sun goes down.

Club Revelin is a Dubrovnik institution, so don’t miss it as you cruise into this World Heritage Site. This one-of-a-kind venue dates back to the 16th century and features both a historical vibe and a contemporary nightlife scene. Those interested in history and a good time will find Revelin’s lineup of world-class DJs, theme nights, and live performances irresistible.

In the heart of the charming city of Split lies Central Club – an exclusive haven for the most discerning of travellers. After a day of cruising on your superyacht, dock in the historic city and immerse yourself in the luxurious ambiance and exclusive clientele that this posh establishment is renowned for. Sip on premium cocktails while indulging in the breathtaking light shows and world-class entertainment, making Central Club the ultimate destination for experiencing the vibrant Croatian nightlife.

Indulge in the lavishness of Noa Beach Club on Pag Island – a magnet for the elite clientele and an epitome of opulent partying. Boasting a picturesque oceanic vista, the VIP cabanas and the floating dance floor set the tone for a splendid soirée. Bask under the sun or sway to the beats of renowned DJs; Noa Beach Club promises an unrivalled extravagance on a yacht charter in Croatia.

destinations.name: Cyprus
destinations.summary: Ideal for yacht charter, Cyprus has two distinct personalities, divided between its southern Greek Cypriot territory and the northern Turkish Cypriot land.
destinations.metaDescription: Ideal for yacht charter, Cyprus has two distinct personalities, divided between its southern Greek Cypriot territory and the northern Turkish Cypriot land.
destinations.lede: The third largest island in the Mediterranean Sea after Sicily and Sardinia, Cyprus has two distinct personalities. Chartering a yacht in Cyprus offers a chance to explore both the southern Greek Cypriot territory and the northern Turkish Cypriot land.
paragraphs: Offering everything from luxurious mountain resorts to scenic fishing villages, and being the reputed birthplace of Aphrodite, Cyprus is often lauded as one of the best superyacht charter destinations in the Mediterranean. The sub-tropical climate means this is one of the hottest places in the Med, and the island enjoys more than double the sunshine hours of northern Europe, so there’s no better way of exploring than on a luxury yacht.

There are three notable nature reserves on Cyprus. For hiking and biking in the summer, head to the Troodos National Forest Park – which in the winter months doubles as a low-key ski resort. Scenic trails weave through the densely forested landscapes of the Akamas Nature Reserve, while White Rocks is where you can discover the island’s most secluded beaches.

With its many bars and clubs, Ayia Napa is a popular choice for the younger generation, while elsewhere the sophisticated dining scene is ubiquitous. Alternatively enjoy a delicious meal on board prepared by your trained chef using fresh local ingredients.
Combining fantastic weather, ancient cultures and modern amenities, Cyprus is an ideal year-round yachting destination.

destinations.lede: From the sun-drenched Côte D’Azur to the historic Loire Valley and the snow-capped peaks of Chamonix, France offers a remarkable diversity of experiences that cater to every taste.
paragraphs: This country, akin to a well-aged Burgundy, boasts not only depth and complexity but a style that is effortlessly chic and timeless.

A South of France luxury yacht charter represents peak style and sophistication. Here, one can glide past the grand belle époque facades, dock beneath Monaco's soaring cliffs and opulent casinos, or find solace in the secluded coves of Porquerolles. This region, a tapestry of chic resort towns and picturesque fishing villages of St Tropez and Portofino stand as a beacon of elegance, offering access to the finest in gourmet dining and high fashion. The Côte D’Azur is not just a destination but a lifestyle, where the Cannes Film Festival and Club 55 are mere highlights in a season of perpetual glamour.

For culture vultures, Provance and the Loire Valley present an opportunity to step into a living storybook. The region is dotted with villages that seem to have leapt from the pages of history, and châteaux that whisper tales of bygone eras.

Wine enthusiasts will find their haven here, with ample opportunities to taste the region's renowned vintages. Meanwhile, the French Alps offer another facet of France's diverse landscape. Resorts like Chamonix provide not just breathtaking vistas but also some of the world’s most coveted ski slopes.

Starting a yacht charter in France opens a gateway to the broader Mediterranean. From this central vantage point, travellers can set off eastward to explore the rugged beauty of Corsica and Sardinia or the dramatic cliffs of the Amalfi Coast. To the west, Spain and the Balearic Islands beckon with their vibrant cultures and stunning coastlines.

destinations.name: Greece
destinations.summary: Sail through the Cyclades and Ionian Islands by superyacht. Ocean Independence arranges Greek island-hopping charters. Enquire for routes and availability.
destinations.metaTitle: Greece Yacht Charter: Aegean to Ionian | Ocean Independence
destinations.metaDescription: Sail through the Cyclades and Ionian Islands by superyacht. Ocean Independence arranges Greek island-hopping charters. Enquire for routes and availability.
paragraphs: A Greece yacht charter is a private, crewed cruise through the Greek islands, with a choice of motor yachts, sailing yachts and catamarans. This page covers where to sail, when to go, the yachts available and what a charter costs. It suits families, first-time charter guests and experienced sailors alike. With around 6,000 islands and islets, more than 250 days of sunshine a year and the warm welcome Greeks call filoxenia, few places reward time on the water more.

Charter a yacht in Greece along the longest coastline in the Mediterranean, where the rugged shores, dense beaches and coastal villages of the mainland are an echo to the wealth of maritime history and ancient tradition.

Greece, a cornerstone of Mediterranean learning, culture, and aesthetics for millennia, has experienced inevitable transformations. Yet, the enduring essence of filoxenia, Greece's unique form of hospitality, deeply ingrained and viewed as a moral duty, remains constant. The country captivates with its spectacular beauty, vibrant hues, and rich historical heritage. However, what distinguishes Greece is the authentic warmth and welcome extended to visitors, making every encounter memorable.

A Greece yacht charter offers more than blue seas and white beaches. You will uncover a mesmerising blend of ancient allure and modern appeal. With its rich historical context, sprawling from the storied mainland to the diverse islands near the Turkish coast, Greece provides an unmatched setting for those seeking to cruise by sea. The nation's waters, home to a myriad of islands grouped into distinct clusters, present a unique cruising experience that is both diverse and captivating.

destinations.name: Italy
destinations.summary: Explore Italy by private superyacht: from the Amalfi Coast and Cinque Terre to Sicily and Sardinia. Luxury crewed charters tailored by OI experts.

destinations.lede: One of those rare but must-do experiences in life is to discover Italy. Renowned for its unparalleled natural, architectural, and culinary wonders, Italy boasts more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.
paragraphs: Its profound historical and cultural impact has cemented it among the Western world's most influential nations. This rich heritage makes Italy a bucket list destination, with coastal regions that offer a taste of elegant Italian living for those exploring by superyacht.

On an Italy yacht charter you're privy to secluded coves, crystal-clear waters, and panoramic views that frame the nation’s diverse landscapes and picturesque harbours. Luxury yacht charters in Italy are less about extravagance and more about accessing the heart of Italian culture in a way that few other experiences can.

It's the blend of Italy's rich history, from its art and architecture to its fashion and food, with jaw-dropping natural beauty that makes a yacht charter here so compelling. The convenience of docking near major cities or drifting beside rolling vineyards means every stop enriches your experience of Italy's layered heritage.

destinations.name: Malta
destinations.summary: Charter a crewed yacht in Malta and cruise the Grand Harbour at Valletta, Gozo and the Blue Lagoon at Comino. We arrange Maltese charters year round.
destinations.metaTitle: Malta Yacht Charter: Valletta, Gozo and the Blue Lagoon
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Malta and cruise the Grand Harbour at Valletta, Gozo and the Blue Lagoon at Comino. We arrange Maltese charters year round.
destinations.lede: At the centre of the Mediterranean Sea, the tiny island cluster of Malta, Gozo and Comino has been an important crossroads for sailors for centuries and is now a popular destination with well-heeled travellers. A Malta Yacht Charter is the ultimate way to explore these beautiful islands.
paragraphs: Lying 60 miles south of Sicily, Malta’s reputation is one of megalithic temples, ancient Hypogeums, fortified cities with towering walls and staggering architecture. Malta packs such a historical punch that its capital, Valletta, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

However, it’s not all history. The island has a thriving yachting community. Party at Portomaso Marina, where the cappuccinos rival Italy’s finest, then retreat to the luxury surroundings of your private yacht.

Paceville is as nocturnal as Barcelona, but without the pretensions. Indulge in excellent dining around Grand Harbour, Europe’s largest natural harbour, which has a spectacular backdrop of limestone fortifications. Make sure to try a fenkata during your private yacht charter in Malta, a traditional stew of rabbit in garlic.

Set sail to escape the heat of the summer and explore deserted beaches and the eerie moonscapes of weather-worn limestone. Anchor offshore and dive fascinating shipwrecks, swim through caves, and fish off the back of the boat on your Malta yacht charter. Alternatively, tuck into Selmun or St Paul’s Bay for some secluded beach walks and a chance to explore the countryside, decorated with wild flowers.

destinations.name: Montenegro
destinations.summary: Chartering a luxury yacht is the very best way to discover Montenegro’s remote islands and unspoiled coastline in the warm waters of the Adriatic.
destinations.metaDescription: Chartering a luxury yacht is the very best way to discover Montenegro’s remote islands and unspoiled coastline in the warm waters of the Adriatic.
destinations.lede: Montenegro, whose name translates to ‘black mountain’, boasts a rich cultural heritage, wonderful variety of landscapes and an unspoiled coastline, perfect for a yacht charter.
paragraphs: Located in the Balkans on the Adriatic Sea, Montenegro’s interior is punctuated by the most rugged mountains in Europe, whilst the scenic coastline is peppered with historic monuments, walled medieval towns and a stunning riviera. Chartering a luxury yacht is the very best way to discover Montenegro’s remote islands and famed UNESCO World Heritage sites . Drop anchor and go kayaking, diving and snorkelling between the small islands or take a romantic stroll through the cobbled streets of ancient villages.

Enjoy authentic food in small family-owned restaurants; in coastal regions, traditional dishes have a Mediterranean focus with cured meats, breads and priganice (fritters) being distinctly Italian in heritage. For dinner, head to the restaurant at the Conte Hotel – a striking residence on the seafront of Perast in Boka Bay, or eat fresh fish caught that morning and grilled on board by your private chef. Once you have discovered this unique yacht charter destination, you are likely to want to return again and again.

destinations.lede: When it comes to superyacht charter, the rich culture, vibrant cuisine, and stunning coastline surrounding Spain is what makes it one of the most sought-after destinations.
paragraphs: Exploring this country by sea is a mouth-watering prospect. And if you're looking for an unforgettable experience, there's no better place to start than Catalonia.

Adopt a more laissez-faire approach to travel and revel in its open, receptive culture filled with unique activities and natural beauty. Take a hot air balloon ride above La Garrotxa Volcanic Zone Natural Park to marvel at 360-degree views of the 40 volcanic cones and 20 lava flows that make up this incredible landscape, or go back in time while touring the preserved mediaeval town of Besalu. A fascinating site to explore, with its collection of churches and civil buildings, you’ll get a glimpse into this country’s captivating past.

While the peak of the charter season in Spain is during the summer months, autumn is a wonderful time to explore the region while cruising on a sailing yacht. The temperatures are a little cooler, yet still very comfortable, and the sea is still warm. Plus, the crowds are not as large in popular tourist spots, making it easier to secure berths.

Whether you're looking for adventure, relaxation, or a little bit of both, a private superyacht charter in Spain offers a memorable experience. Expect the unexpected at every turn – from the surreal, Art Nouveau creations of Antoni Gaudí to setting sail for the Balearics – on a luxury private yacht charter in Spain you’ll create memories that will last a lifetime.
