destinations.lede: For yacht charter guests, Sardinia is not just a destination to experience the pinnacle of Mediterranean elegance. From lounging on the deck against a backdrop of Liscia Ruja's pink sands to exploring the vibrant streets of Cagliari by night, every aspect of Sardinia promises an unparalleled yachting vacation.
paragraphs: Sardinia oozes luxury and is a true superyacht charter haven. It enjoys light, constant breezes, making it somewhat cooler than much of the Mediterranean in summer. Elevated to exclusivity in the '60s when the Aga Khan invested in the Costa Smeralda, turning it into an eco-playground paradise for his friends, the area has relatively few traditional farms and in their place, lavish villas overlook the bays lined with superyachts during the summer. The Costa Smeralda is now legendary. Take time to watch the world go by as you sip an espresso on the waterfront at Porto Cervo and dine in one of Cala di Volpe's sophisticated restaurants during your yacht charter in Sardinia.

Those who rate peace and tranquillity over people-watching may prefer to set sail for the quiet shores of La Maddalena. Like a more rugged version of the Caribbean, the seven main isles in the Maddalena National Park form a stunning archipelago for yacht charter, offering a magical mix of history, scenery and true Italian charm. Don’t miss Porto Rotondo’s luxurious port with its granite amphitheatre and the church of San Lorenzo and in Cagliari the impressive Castello offers spectacular views.

The northeastern coast, home to the famed Emerald Coast, is a mosaic of glittering beaches, exclusive resorts, and upscale boutiques, particularly around Porto Cervo. Famously fashionable, the marina is lined with sophisticated cafes, high-end shops, and world class restaurants, creating one of the finest destinations for a luxury yacht charter in the Mediterranean.

Sardinia's cultural tapestry is equally compelling, with ancient archaeological sites like the ruins of Nora and Tharros offering a glimpse into the island's rich past. The mediaeval city of Alghero, with its Catalan heritage, presents a fascinating exploration of history and architecture.

Gastronomy is another pillar of the Sardinian luxury charter experience. The island's cuisine is a celebration of its maritime and agricultural heritage, offering dishes that range from the decadence of lobsters to the simplicity of pane carasau. Local vineyards complement these culinary delights with exquisite wines, enhancing the island's gastronomic appeal.

destinations.name: Sicily
destinations.summary: Separated from Europe by the Strait of Messina and lapped by the Ionian Sea, the picturesque yachting destination of Sicily is the largest of the Italian islands.
destinations.metaDescription: A Sicily yacht charter offers access to gorgeous clear blue waters, lush mountains and the delights of chic cities. Explore our insider guide here.
destinations.lede: Separated from Europe by the Strait of Messina and lapped by the Ionian Sea, the picturesque yachting destination of Sicily is the largest of the Italian islands. Charter a crewed luxury motor yacht or sailing boat with Ocean Independence and explore the island of Sicily and all the beauty that it offers.
paragraphs: Known as much for its mafia past as its grumbling volcano, Mount Etna, the island offers huge variety for a summer Sicily yacht charter – from the clear blue waters and lush, verdant mountains to the chic cities and hillside villages. Greek tyrants, Byzantine bishops, Arab emirs and Norman Knights all gave Sicily its diversity.

Palermo, the old town of Sicily’s capital, is absolutely stunning; a terracotta-walled rabbit warren of cobbled streets with hanging baskets trailing flame-red flowers. Catania is a paradise for adventurers and hikers, as is the UNESCO-protected World Heritage site around Etna, Europe’s tallest and largest active volcano, which can be perfectly observed from your private yacht charter in Sicily.

The rolling countryside in the south throws up the precariously balanced hilltop towns of Ragusa Ibla and Erice, though you’ll keep coming back to Taormina. As the heat rises, retreat to Gran Duca for a bottle of chilled local Nero d’Avola (viticulture is a big thing in Sicily, however don’t expect a broad selection of international wines) and a generous plate of spicy spaghetti al vongole while sitting high above the bay to see your crewed motor yacht or sailing boat at anchor below you.

Cruise the Mediterranean Sea around the Aeolian islands of Vulcano, Salina and Lipari and explore everything from lava formations to cliff-top meadows and deserted white sand beaches during your Sicily yacht charter.

destinations.name: Venice
destinations.summary: A city of immense historical importance and exquisite beauty, Venice is evergreen in popularity and a great location to visit during an eastern Italy yacht charter.
destinations.metaTitle: Venice Yacht Charter: Cruise the Lagoon and the Adriatic
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Venice and cruise the lagoon, Burano and the Adriatic coast, with Croatia within easy reach. Our consultants plan the route.
destinations.lede: A city of immense historical importance and exquisite beauty, Venice is evergreen in popularity and a great location to visit during an eastern Italy yacht charter.
paragraphs: A huge draw for visitors, Venice remains highly popular for the diverse sights on display. Impressive and important buildings are ubiquitous, piazzas, walkways, ornate buildings and palaces at every turn are a spectacular sight. Visit lively St Mark’s Square to soak up the atmosphere – flanked by St Mark’s Basilica, the ornate Doge’s Palace and the Torre dell’Orologio, this is the perfect place to start your tour of Venice. An important historic historic landmark, the Bridge of Sighs connects the Prigioni Nuove to the Doge’s Palace. Legend states that as criminals were taken from the palace over the bridge, they’d cast a final glimpse back at Venice and sigh, considering their final punishment.

With hundreds of canals connecting the various islands making up the city, the largest and most famous is the Canale Grande. An important waterway for hundreds of years, it passes from one side of Venice to the other, with only four bridges spanning it. The canal is lined by over 170 buildings dating from as early as the 13th century and populated by consistently busy water traffic.

Art enthusiasts will enjoy the Gallerie dell’Accademia, hosting a fine collection of Renaissance masterpieces by artists such as Titian and Canaletto, while Murano is another island within the Venice district famed for glass blowing and glass products.

Offering a different experience from the country’s western Mediterranean coast, a yacht charter along the east coast of Italy offers a range of activities. Cruise from Venice and stop at delightful towns along the coast to experience quintessential Italian culture. From historical Ravenna and popular Rimini down to serene Bari in Puglia, Italy’s Adriatic coast offers exceptional cruising.

Built on a lagoon, Venice comprises over 100 tiny islands, divided by canals and connected by bridges. The unique construction and architecture give the Italian city more than its share of romance. As the world’s only pedestrian city, Venice is a sensory overload: from the mosaic encrusted Basilica di San Marco, to the Museo Querini Stampalia crammed with Renaissance paintings. It is, without a doubt, the most photogenic city in Europe and must be explored when chartering a yacht in eastern Italy. Explore the labyrinth of canals, wander the atmospheric cobbled streets, marvel at the iconic Renaissance architecture and visit the skilled glass blowers of Murano.

From Venice, you’re within a day’s sail of the Croatian coast. But if it’s Italy that you want to explore, head south along the east coast to discover the fabulous beaches and villages along the Adriatic coastline. Stop in Rimini for an alfresco snack at Casina del Bosco where you can enjoy some of the best and most diverse piadine in town, served with sensational fillings such as caramelised figs. Visit Ravenna, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site with captivating monuments and mosaics. In Puglia, Bari offers the chance to indulge in simple but delicious cuisine and relish the lilting fishing villages of this magical sun-baked stretch of southeast Italy.

destinations.name: Budva
destinations.summary: Characterised by narrow streets and quaint squares, medieval buildings and stony churches, Budva is a stunning yacht charter destination on the Montenegrin Adriatic coast.
destinations.metaDescription: Budva is an ancient magnet for inquisitive visitors, bursting with cultural heritage. The narrow streets and quaint squares make this an unmissable destination.
destinations.lede: Characterised by narrow streets and quaint squares, medieval buildings and stony churches, Budva is a stunning yacht charter destination on the Montenegrin Adriatic coast.
paragraphs: Budva is Montenegro’s most popular tourist destination, and a city that should be on every to-do list. The Old Town is a maze of Venetian cobblestone streets and historic monuments, centred around the 15th century citadel.

Known as the “Riviera of Sandy Beaches”, Budva comes alive in the summer months. The beautiful and well-equipped beaches are buzzing with atmosphere, making it a perfect location for yacht charter. Take a tender into one of the beaches, the popular choices being Mogren, Becici and Sveti Stefan, to enjoy the shallow waters or anchor further out and enjoy some watersports. Choose Enjoy relaxing at the Skadar Lake or visiting the Lovcen National Park; if feeling active, enjoy a hike in the mountains of the Durmitor National Park with spectacular glacier lakes and snow-covered peaks – the panoramic views are amazing.

destinations.name: Kotor
destinations.summary: The Bay of Kotor is a must-visit for every tourist. Regarded as one of the most beautiful bays in the region, it offers amazing views to the stunning medieval town of Kotor.
destinations.metaDescription: A hidden gem amongst mountains looking out onto the Adriatic Sea, the medieval town of Kotor is a must-visit destination on a yacht charter in Montenegro.
destinations.lede: The Bay of Kotor is a must-visit for every superyacht. Regarded as one of the most beautiful bays in the region, it offers amazing views over to Kotor, a stunning medieval town with some fascinating local legends.
paragraphs: Stroll past ancient churches, slip into a romantic restaurant or sit outside one of the many bars watching animated locals on their way to dinner.
Nearby the pretty Our Lady of the Rocks island, is well worth a tour and listen to guides recount the legend of the isle. Look out for dolphins when cruising here.

Kotor is a fortified town on Montenegro’s Adriatic coast, in a bay near the limestone cliffs of Mt. Lovćen. Characterized by winding streets and squares, its medieval old town has several Romanesque churches, including Kotor Cathedral. It’s also home to the Maritime Museum, which explores local seafaring history.

destinations.name: The Balearics

flags: site map has 4 pins; using their centroid

destinations.summary: Sun-blushed, celebrity-endorsed and packing scenic punch, the Balearic Islands are among Europe's finest yacht charter holiday destinations.
destinations.metaTitle: Balearics Yacht Charter: Mallorca, Ibiza and Formentera
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in the Balearics and cruise Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera. Our consultants arrange Balearic charters each summer.
destinations.lede: Sun-blushed, celebrity-endorsed and packing scenic punch, the Balearic Islands are among Europe's finest yacht charter holiday destinations.
paragraphs: The Balearic Islands – Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca, and Formentera – are one of Europe's prime island getaways, perfect for a private motor yacht charter. With their 1,723 km of coastline, the Balearics host yachting's holy trinity – golden sand, azure sea, and more sunshine hours than any destination in Italy, Croatia, or the South of France. Their unique beauty is unparalleled, offering pristine beaches, scenic coastlines, and a constantly shifting horizon.

Although famous as the party playground of the Mediterranean, the Spanish archipelago offers much more. Anchor off a serene beach on Formentera for yoga at sunset, or kitesurf off Playa de Llevant. Explore Menorca's quiet coastline by yacht or hop ashore for mountain biking. On Mallorca, visit the hilltop town of Deià, a haven for writers, artists, and bohemians, or explore a maritime nature haven only accessible by boat. Then, when you hanker after high-octane jollity, join Ibiza's party elite for dancing until dawn.

Sun-soaked and skirted by golden sands, take your pick from 375 beaches of the Balearic Islands, like Cala Bóquer, where only goats, starfish, and kayakers make it ashore. Or Playa de Ses Illetes, a twin-sided sandbar where the only beach club is the one on your yacht.

Colourful fishing boats piled high with nets are pulled up on the shore, and glamorous boutiques sit hidden on narrow cobbled lanes. Tapas bars line busy squares, and Michelin star restaurants sit shoreside. Littered with UNESCO World Heritage Sites, destination cities, and wildly competitive gastronomy, the Balearic Islands are vastly different in their separate identities and a highlight of any superyacht charter.

destinations.name: Valencia
destinations.summary: Set sail along the banks of the Turia River during a Valencia yacht charter and discover an ancient city bursting with charm.
destinations.metaDescription: Discover the cultural delights of southern Spain and explore the crystal waters of the Mediterranean on a Valencia yacht charter.
destinations.lede: Set sail along the banks of the Turia River during a Valencia yacht charter and discover an ancient city bursting with charm. Now a stop for the Volvo Ocean race and host to multiple sailing weeks, yachting enthusiasts flock to this beautiful port, and for good reason.
paragraphs: To get your bearings, stroll the 4 kilometre long Paseo Marítimo, a beautiful palm-tree-lined promenade. The port itself was completely remodelled for the 32nd America’s Cup, while the Medieval architecture of the old city is retained in pockets. Highlights include the San Miguel de Los Reyes Monastery and the ancient Towers of the Medieval city, which afford stunning views across the city to the Mediterranean Sea.

Don’t miss the Las Fallas festival in March during your Valencia luxury yacht charter, which begins with spectacular fireworks. The Holy Week celebrations held in Valencia are also considered among the most intensely colourful in Spain. During August, crowds are drawn to the nearby town of Buñol by “La Tomatina” for the annual tomato fight, which makes a fascinating spectacle. Make sure you leave time during a private yacht charter in Valencia to visit Albufera, a beautiful freshwater lagoon and estuary that is a natural park perfect for bird watching and hiking. Golfers should hit the greens at El Saler, El Bosque, Manises, and the Club Escorpión.

destinations.name: Göcek
destinations.summary: The Gulf of Göcek on the Lycian coast is one of Turkey's most alluring charter destinations. Crystal clear waters abound with marine life and the majestic peaks run down to lush emerald pine forests.
destinations.metaTitle: Gocek Yacht Charter: Twelve Islands on the Lycian Coast
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Gocek and cruise the Twelve Islands, sheltered pine-fringed bays and the Lycian coast. Our consultants plan the route.
destinations.lede: The Gulf of Göcek on Turkey’s Lycian coast is one of the country’s most alluring charter destinations. Crystal clear waters abound with marine life and the majestic peaks run down to lush emerald pine forests.
paragraphs: There are many beautiful anchorages and attractions in the Göcek/Fethiye area so you can spend the week just pottering around. The prevailing wind is from the west and tends to blow a little stronger in the afternoons, so if you want to go further afield, the Bozburun peninsular is within a reasonable distance with a marina in Marmaris en route. In Göcek, fishing villages sit below dramatic rock faces and gorgeous beaches with shallow waters offer excellent snorkelling terrain. For sun-worshippers, the coastline is scattered with pristine beaches, from sands of Sarigerme or the Inclice beach, surrounded by dense pine woodland.

But it’s not all slow living. For those who want to get the adrenalin coursing, consider a wild water ride in the Saklikent, Turkey’s longest and deepest gorge and an insanely beautiful spot. Furthermore, the favourable winds here mean the Gulf of Gocek is a paradise for paragliders. The town of Göcek still has the lilt of a traditional fishing village, despite the fact that is has slowly and quietly emerged as Turkey’s superyacht hub, with magnificent marinas and all the amenities a seasoned traveller expects. An archipelago of gorgeous islands pepper the gulf, each with their individual charm, but all featuring postcard beaches as well as secluded anchorages and the opportunity to try out your yachts toys: from jet skiing to scuba diving.

destinations.name: Marmaris
destinations.summary: Marmaris is framed by rugged mountains and has a reputation for being a cosmopolitan hub, particularly attractive to yachting enthusiasts with one of the most impressive natural harbours in the world.
destinations.metaTitle: Marmaris Yacht Charter: Turkish Riviera Natural Harbour
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Marmaris and cruise one of the finest natural harbours in the world, gateway to the Datca and Hisaronu gulfs. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: A former fishing village,in the Mugla Province of southwest Turkey, Marmaris is framed by rugged mountains and has a reputation for being a cosmopolitan hub. It is particularly attractive to yachting enthusiasts thanks to one of the most impressive natural harbours in the world.
paragraphs: Living up to its name in every sense, the translation for Marmaris is “shining”. The city is a labyrinth of bazaars, fine dining restaurants and chichi bars and clubs: a microcosm of modern Turkey. With wild, mountainous terrain and dense pine forests, it is also a paradise for hiking and outdoor enthusiasts. Adventure-hungry visitors can explore on mountain bikes or quad bikes, with both easy and more challenging routes to choose from. Or why not try horse riding through the countryside, and experience the scenery at a slower pace.

The coast around Marmaris is known for gorgeous beaches, with Cleopatra Beach – allegedly her wedding present from Mark Anthony – being the most famed. The icing-sugar sand beach of Iclemer is an ideal spot for families with its gentle slopes and shallow waters. Cruise along the coast to create your own breeze in summer, have lunch on board and cool off by diving and snorkeling in one of the many small bays where the marine life is rich and plentiful and the water is crystal clear

destinations.name: The Galapagos Islands
destinations.summary: Found off the coast of Equador, the Galapagos are a showcase of evolution amidst unspoiled natural beauty. Take time to indulge in the peace and calm of one of the most remote spots on the planet.
destinations.metaDescription: A luxury yacht charter in the Galapagos Islands offers the chance to discover unspoiled natural beauty and hugely diverse wildlife both on land and at sea.
destinations.lede: Found off the coast of Ecuador, visit the Galapagos for a showcase of evolution in unspoiled natural beauty whilst indulging in the peace and calm of one of the most remote spots on the planet. Not all of these volcanic islands are open to tourists and some can only be visited by guided, licensed boats.
paragraphs: Despite their sometimes barren appearance, Charles Darwin’s “Enchanted Isles” are, without a doubt, one of the most magical places on the planet. The rugged coastline is interspersed with cactus forests, pristine beaches, hidden coves and quiet bays that are perfect for any seasoned traveller seeking natural tranquility.

One of the main highlights is the remarkable wildlife encountered here, including colourful crabs, bustling penguins, proud flamingos and a vast array of species found nowhere else in the world. Approximately half of the species living here are indigenous and wholly unique to this small archipelago, making conservation and protection all the more important. For this reason, access to the islands is only granted to visitors accompanied by guides, in order to preserve this natural wonderland for generations to come. This is the ultimate holiday destination for animal lovers.

Underwater, the bounty of life is equally exciting. Experienced divers will revel in a world filled with marine life that is encouraged by an amalgamation of colder currents from Antarctica and warmer ones from the Pacific. Large and vibrant fish, ranging from hammerhead sharks to eagle rays make a dive here a singularly extraordinary experience. Equally, the waters can be explored by snorkelling for those less accustomed to the somewhat difficult diving conditions.

Unsurprisingly, the most popular activities in the Galapagos are snorkelling, scuba diving and guided tours. With white beaches and great swells, there is also plenty of surfing, swimming and sunbathing to do. For those that prefer a more relaxed pace, the tourist hub of Puerto Ayora (Santa Cruz Island) also offers great shopping, fine restaurants and luxury hotels.

destinations.name: Dominica
destinations.summary: Dominica forms part of the Lesser Antilles archipelago and is considered a wilderness of natural beauty, with crashing waterfalls, glistening springs and more than 300 radiant rivers to explore.
destinations.metaDescription: The Commonwealth of Dominica forms part of the archipelago of the Lesser Antilles and is a superb option for yacht charter in the Caribbean.
destinations.lede: The Commonwealth of Dominica forms part of the archipelago of the Lesser Antilles and is considered a wilderness of natural beauty, with crashing waterfalls, glistening springs and more than 300 radiant rivers waiting to be explored. It is an up and coming yachting destination, though it’s mostly anchorages.
paragraphs: With rare species of plants, animals and especially birds, this is a paradise for naturalists. Many make a pilgrimage here to see the Sisserou parrot. Found only on Dominica, it is the island’s national bird and features on the flag. Hike to the country’s highest point, Morne Diablotins, or stay on board and try and seek out the whales. The clear azure waters surrounding Dominica are home to an abundance of whale species.

Dominica is still being formed by geothermal-volcanic activity and has an impressive hot spring, Boiling Lake, which is an awesome sight. As a result the marine life means excellent scuba diving and snorkelling. Culturally, Dominica is famed for its musical festivals Creole in the Park and the World Creole Music Festival, which are full of folklore, colour and music. A yachting holiday on Dominica is a unique experience of simply astounding natural beauty paired with a gentle climate and a sense of pure calm and relaxation.

destinations.name: Martinique
destinations.summary: Politically and culturally, Martinique in the Windward Islands is more French than Caribbean and is famed for its hiking and wreck diving in the clear, turquoise waters teeming with marine life.
destinations.metaDescription: Politically and culturally, Martinique in the Windward Islands is more French than Caribbean and is home to turquoise waters teeming with marine life.
destinations.lede: Politically and culturally, Martinique in the Windward Islands is more French than Caribbean and is famed for its hiking and wreck diving in the clear, turquoise waters teeming with marine life.
paragraphs: A seamless blend of Caribbean and French influence, Martinique fascinates with a dual personality. To the north, volcanic Mont Pelée rises proudly amidst rugged, rainforest-clad terrain, while the south boasts sandy swathes and sparkling water – a nirvana for sun worshippers. Swim off the flawless beaches or snorkel alongside turtles feeding on sea grass, while colourful fish dart amongst rocky outcrops.
Head east for an exhilarating kiteboarding and surfing experience, where you’ll also find the capital, Fort-de-France, with its excellent restaurants, chic boutiques and exclusive nightclubs.

In the bay of Saint-Pierre many ships were sunk by the eruption of the Mont Pelée volcano in 1902 and the wrecks are intriguing and eerie. Another popular spot for divers is Nahoon, a three-mast boat lying off the coast under only 36m of water: you may even be able to see it from aboard your yacht.
Choose your slice of Martinique: secluded beaches or gorgeous waterfalls, or explore both by circumnavigating the island.

destinations.name: Calvi
destinations.summary: Calvi is a beautiful port town on the Mediterranean coast of Corsica. It is situated at the base of a large mountain, and has been an important trade centre for centuries.
destinations.metaTitle: Calvi Yacht Charter: Corsican Citadel, Bays and Beaches
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Calvi and arrive by sea beneath the Genoese citadel, with pine-backed bays along the Balagne coast. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: Calvi is a beautiful port town on the Mediterranean coast of Corsica. It is situated at the base of a large mountain, and has been an important trade centre for centuries.
paragraphs: A luxury yacht charter is the ideal way to fully appreciate the beauty of Calvi’s magnificent setting. Framed by rising mountains topped with green forests, the sandy beaches line the arc of the bay, while colourful fishing boats bob in the palm-tree fringed marina. Ashore the meandering maze of cobbled streets packed with shops, cafes and restaurants offer delight for shoppers and coffee-lovers alike.

For those with a penchant for history, head up to the 15th century citadel and the Cathedrale St-Jean-Baptiste at the highest point. Soak up magnificent views of the red-tiled town and over the bay as the sun sets. During the busy summer months, Calvi is alive with the sound of music thanks to a series of festivals and concerts in the citadel and around the town – and on 15 August enjoy an impressive fireworks display aboard your superyacht charter offering breathtaking views of Calvi. With plenty to do in the area, nature lovers will enjoy a trip down the coast to the Scandola World Heritage Site, strewn with dramatic cliff formations and sea stacks, not to mention home to diverse marine life. Quai Landry links the marina and the port, and is a great place to get a feel for the town and watch the world go by. Past the promenade, lush la Pinède forest stretches along the back of the beach bordering Calvi bay, underlining the frontier between land and sea.

Calvi’s 6km of glittering beach, simply oozes style of a French Riviera resort, offering gently shelving, warm, protected waters, ideal for families. With a fine array of waterfront restaurants, some of which serve directly onto the beach, visitors will never go hungry. Nearby Arinella Plage at Lumio is a small sandy stretch with stunning views across the bay to the citadel, this is an ideal bay to drop anchor to benefit from the shelter of rocky headlands and a popular spot to snorkel.

destinations.name: Antibes
destinations.summary: This is the picture-postcard Riviera, from the pine-fringed coastline to the golden beaches. As a central hub for the yachting community, Antibes is one of the largest pleasure ports and home to some
destinations.metaTitle: Antibes Yacht Charter: Old Town, Cap and Superyacht Quay
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Antibes and cruise Cap d Antibes, the old town ramparts and the largest superyacht quay on the Riviera. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: This is the picture-postcard Riviera, from the pine-fringed coastline to the golden beaches. As a central hub for the yachting community, Antibes is one of the largest pleasure ports and home to some of the most impressive yachts in the world.
paragraphs: Cap d’Antibes is a great day anchorage – during your Antibes yacht charter indulge in a morning dip before taking the tender to shore for lunch at the iconic Hotel du Cap Eden Rock. Picasso once lived in Antibes and was reputedly captivated by the views and the nostalgic glamour: it is well worth taking a visit to the Museé Picasso to see some of his most iconic works.

Within the quaint, cobbled streets of the old town it is easy to re-imagine the old fishing village of Antibes. Wind your way to upscale La Taille de Guepe and relish the intimate setting and sublime food. Panoramic views from the Phare de la Garoupe lighthouse are sensational. Explore small coves, private castles and the exquisite beauty of the Sentier des Douaniers during your Antibes superyacht charter. For those who prefer the ease of marina life, Port Vauban is Europe’s largest, offering plenty of berthing for superyachts over 60m (and earning Antibes the nickname Billionaires’ Quay).

destinations.name: Cannes
destinations.summary: Considered the heart of the Cote d'Azur, the world-famous seaside resort of Cannes oozes exclusive glamour like nowhere else on earth.
destinations.metaTitle: Cannes Yacht Charter: The Croisette, Lerins and Festivals
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Cannes and berth off the Croisette for the Film Festival or Yachting Festival, with the Lerins Islands close by. Enquire now.
destinations.lede: Considered the heart of the Cote d'Azur, Cannes oozes exclusive glamour like nowhere else on earth.
paragraphs: Falling neatly between Nice, Antibes, Monaco and St. Tropez, Cannes is home to the Cannes Film Festival, held in May, where celebrities take over the town, attending lavish ceremonies and parties at a handful of discreet venues. When the sun sets everyone spills out into one of countless Michelin Star restaurants, where Mediterranean food and wine commands serious prices and excellent reviews. The pavements are lined with beautiful people sharing platters of succulent shellfish and bottles of ice-cold rosé.

The legendary La Croisette will satisfy your shopping needs during your Cannes yacht charter. It is the perfect destination for shoppers, with every conceivable independent boutique and couture house lining the boulevard. For the food lovers, make sure to explore Le Suquet where you can wander into local eateries without booking and find some of the finest, most authentic regional and international cuisine. Nearby, the Isles des Lérins, off mainland Cannes, are an ideal place to drop anchor and spend a relaxing afternoon during your Cannes luxury yacht charter. The fort on the larger island is reputed to have held Dumas’ Man in the Iron Mask. There is also a monastery to visit on Ile St Honorat, belonging to Cistercian monks who produce exquisite wines, honey and lavender oil.

destinations.name: Cap Ferrat
destinations.summary: Enjoying a position between Monaco and Nice, Cap Ferrat is notable for its clutch of exclusive hotels, restaurants and beach clubs, and ideally placed for quick access to Cote d'Azur hotspots.
destinations.metaDescription: Cap Ferrat is notable for its clutch of exclusive hotels, restaurants and beach clubs, and ideally placed for quick access to Cote d'Azur hotspots.
destinations.lede: Enjoying a position between Monaco and Nice, Cap Ferrat is notable for its clutch of exclusive hotels, restaurants and beach clubs, and ideally placed for quick access to Cote d'Azur hotspots.
paragraphs: Providing a great anchorage, St Jean Cap Ferrat, located near Villefranche, is a ragged headland where substantial private homes are just visible from the water. Long, languid days can be spent swimming off the aft deck, diving in the incredible waters and snoozing on the beaches – themselves a catwalk of beauty and glamour.

If the mood takes you, the Villa Ephrussi is a fascinating afternoon excursion. This hilltop palace offers stunning views from the Cap and was once home to Baroness Rothschild in the Belle Époque era. With a combination of Spanish, French and Japanese influences, it plays host to an outstanding art collection and the gardens are spectacular. St Jean Harbour and Promenade Maurice Rouvier offer excellent yacht spotting and the ideal place for an evening stroll before ducking into one of the many exceptional fish restaurants.

Perhaps first enjoy a glass of wine among the locals at Le Cadillac or La Civette. With a backdrop of rich terracotta rooftops among beautiful tiered gardens, this relaxed and exclusive enclave is one for the pocket book of the discerning yacht charterer. The peninsula is part of the Pelagos Sanctuary for Mediterranean Marine Mammals, a protected area jointly managed by France, Monaco and Italy, making it a prime spot for diving as well as whale and dolphin watching.

destinations.name: Eze
destinations.summary: Head up above the azure Med for cool countryside chic. Perched on a rocky peak the ancient village of Eze is centered around a 12th century castle with stunning panoramic views from the top.
destinations.metaTitle: Eze Yacht Charter: Riviera Hilltop Village and Coastline
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht at Eze and anchor below the most striking perched village on the Riviera, set between Nice and Monaco. Our consultants advise.
destinations.lede: Escape the seaside and explore the beauty of the French countryside during your Eze yacht charter. Perched on a rocky peak, the ancient village of Eze is centered around a 12th century castle with stunning panoramic views from the top. With a single point of access and exit through the vaulted Potern entry, this pretty village sits above the busy Moyenne Corniche.
paragraphs: Wander the intricate labyrinth of medieval streets, bursting with craft boutiques, art exhibitions and lively cafes. High up, the renowned Jardin Exotique overlooks magnificent villas adorned with vibrant bougainvillea: a veritable horticulturalists’ dream, over 400 cacti, citrus trees and tropical plants encircle the castle ruins.

Tucked away, the enchanting and ancient Chateau Eza is one of the most visually stunning hotels along the Cote d’Azur. A former residence to a Swedish Prince, private balconies and terraces in the 14 intimate suites offer epic vistas: during your Eze luxury yacht charter adventure, have lunch in the gourmet restaurant on one of the terraces overlooking the sparkling sea. At the top of Eze village beyond the stone walls is the Chateau de la Chèvre d’Or; also one of the world’s finest hotels. The Moroccan-style gardens link to streams of beautiful terraces dropping down towards the sea, set amongst serene courtyards, swimming pools and sundecks. Inside guests marvel at the giant chandeliers, Italian marble and Parisian antiques: no wonder the spacious suites have hosted Marlene Dietrich and Robert de Niro. Coffee on the terrace, soaking up the ultimate Mediterranean view, is highly recommended.

A special surprise awaits visitors to Eze in the form of the Galimard Perfume Factory and Museum. Enjoy a unique opportunity to take part in the perfumery workshop, fascinating behind-the-scenes tour of the lab and factory, plus regular demonstrations. Here nostalgia is captured in antique perfume bottles abundantly displayed in this magical environment, take a chance to purchase aromatic products from this unforgettable haven of olfactory delights.

destinations.name: Monaco
destinations.summary: An iconic yacht charter destination, the tiny principality of Monaco, between Nice to the west and the north Italian coast, is an independent sovereign state ruled by Prince Albert II of the Grimaldi
destinations.metaTitle: Monaco Yacht Charter: Port Hercule, Grand Prix and More
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Monaco and berth at Port Hercule for the Grand Prix or the Yacht Show. Our consultants arrange Monaco charters year round.
destinations.lede: An iconic yacht charter destination, the tiny principality of Monaco, between Nice to the west and the north Italian coast, is an independent sovereign state ruled by Prince Albert II of the Grimaldi family.
paragraphs: Monaco’s exclusivity and preferable tax system make it home to some of the world’s largest yachts. For fast paced, glitzy lifestyle, Monte Carlo is the perfect playground for grown-ups who appreciate the finer things in life. From the superyachts lining the marina and the sports cars circling Casino Square to the boutiques – there is nothing understated about this bold enclave of luxury. While cruising on your Monaco yacht charter, take in the stunning anchorages of nearby Cap d’Ail or Cap Ferrat. From Monaco, the Italian Riviera is a natural onwards charter destination.

If partying until dawn is not on the agenda, enjoying an Aperol spritz in Casino Square is recommended. Visit the Oceanographic Museum or the Palace, act like a local and take a dip in the saltwater pool at Port de Hercules where you have a spectacular view over the harbour and the yachts. Plan in advance to attend the Grand Prix in May, where you can watch the race trackside from the back of your Monaco superyacht charter, or attend the Monaco Yacht Show in September.

destinations.name: The Porquerolles
destinations.summary: The three islands of the Porquerolles are renowned for their secret beaches and calm inlets. Turquoise waters, long sandy beaches and palm trees give them a desert island quality.
destinations.metaDescription: The three islands of the Porquerolles are renowned for their secret beaches and calm inlets. Turquoise waters and palm trees give them a desert island quality.
destinations.lede: The three islands of the Porquerolles are renowned for their secret beaches and calm inlets. Turquoise waters, long sandy beaches and palm trees give them a desert island quality.
paragraphs: A world away from the hustle and bustle of the busy coastal towns of the Cote d’Azur, locals play pétanque in bougainvillea-clad squares, while visitors sip Pastis at small cafés and life moves at a slower pace.

The landscape of the Porquerolles is a medley of cliffs, bays, plains and forests, making the islands an perfect place to enjoy activities such as hiking, horse riding and mountain biking. Of course, that’s once you have tired of basking on the bow, anchored off one of the many idyllic white sand beaches.

Vinophiles will enjoy a trip to Domaine Perzinsky, a family-run vineyard offering a wonderful selection of local Porquerolles wine, while sun-worshippers head to crescent-shaped Plage de Notre Dame, where the pearly sand is flanked by fragrant eucalyptus and pine trees whose exotic perfume is carried on the summer breeze. On Iles d’Hyères cars are not allowed so it has retained its natural beauty – bring comfortable shoes so that you can explore.

destinations.name: St Tropez
destinations.summary: Everything visitors look for in a destination can be found in a St Tropez yacht charter: staggering views, a lively social scene, chic shopping and, of course, fabulous beaches.
destinations.metaDescription: Discover the glamour of the Cote d'Azur on a St Tropez yacht charter and indulge in shopping, eating and nightlife. Explore our curated insider guide.
destinations.lede: Everything visitors look for in a destination can be found in a St Tropez yacht charter: staggering views, a lively social scene, chic shopping and, of course, fabulous beaches.
paragraphs: Without a doubt, St. Tropez is the most famous resort on the Cote d’Azur and the town is like a film set. Propelled to fame in the 60’s when Brigitte Bardot frequented its shores, it offers the exceptional of everything.

At its heart St. Tropez is still an old fishing village. Its maritime history and relaxed atmosphere keep it down to earth. Just a few steps behind the opulent boutiques of the main streets, you’ll find old-fashioned butchers’ shops, a morning fish market, and boulangeries. As the sun goes down on the Vieille Ville, gleaming superyachts come back to port and vespas, porsches and mini-mokes zip around, dropping off bejewelled locals.

Party people flock to the iconic bar at Les Caves du Roy at Hotel Byblos for cocktails and music to get the party started. Club 55 on Plage du Pampelonne is the longest running beach club. Established in the 50s, it still draws a chic international crowd. At both locations, the streets are lined with gleaming supercars. If you are looking for definitive glamour against a traditional backdrop, a St Tropez luxury yacht charter is the way to go.

destinations.name: Villefranche
destinations.summary: Villefranche is one of the deepest natural harbours in the Mediterranean and is considered to be amongst the most beautiful in the world.
destinations.metaDescription: Enjoy a luxury yacht charter in Villefranche Sur Mer. Discover unspoiled nature, breathtaking views over the Mediterranean, & a picturesque village. Read more.
destinations.lede: The captivating old town of Villefranche Sur Mer cascades down the hillside and drops to a café-lined shore with a long beach. Anchor in the well-protected bay during a yacht charter in Villefranche Sur Mer and enjoy a relaxing afternoon enjoying this region’s finest sites and attractions.
paragraphs: Villefranche is one of the deepest natural harbours in the Mediterranean and is considered to be amongst the most beautiful in the world. From the town’s fort of Mont Alban, you can see the Italian coastline stretching as far as the eye can see.
Despite its beauty and appeal, Villefranche and its neighbour Beaulieu-Sur-Mer remain relatively unspoiled and are often overlooked by visitors to the Cote d’Azur.

However, those in the know are well aware of the delights that Villefranche offers, making this a wonderful under-the-radar destination. For water enthusiasts, the pretty bay offers plenty of water sports, from sport fishing to diving. If you prefer to watch the action, take a sunbed at Plage de Mariniéres, which boasts beautiful white sand lapped by the blue waters of the Mediterranean Sea.
On the quayside, destination restaurants include La Mére Germaine, which reputedly serves the best soupe de poisson on the Riviera – a must during a luxury yacht charter in Villefranche Sur Mer.

Villefranche Sur Mer is conveniently located between Monaco and Nice, with moorings offering excellent security for large superyachts. Additionally, the surrounding hills are ideal for biking and hiking, offering plenty of trails to choose from. During a Villefranche luxury yacht charter, make sure you leave time to head to the top of Mont Leuze, where you can enjoy spectacular views over the bay.

destinations.name: Mykonos
destinations.summary: As part of the Cyclades islands, Mykonos lies in the centre of the Aegean Sea and is a whitewashed paradise, where mythology and history collide with a cosmopolitan party scene.
destinations.metaTitle: Mykonos Yacht Charter: Cyclades Beaches, Bays, Nightlife
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Mykonos and cruise Aegean beaches by day and the celebrated nightlife by evening, with Delos close by. Enquire today.
paragraphs: As a part of the Cyclades islands, Mykonos lies in the centre of the Aegean Sea and is a whitewashed paradise. Greek mythology and history collide with a cosmopolitan party scene, and you can enjoy the best of the island by chartering a yacht in Mykonos.

Allegedly the location of the great mythic battle between Zeus and the Titans, the island captures the heady allure of this fable. Traditional Cycladic architecture, whitewashed streets and pretty churches are beautifully preserved, as is the quaint harbour in the middle of a wide bay – the perfect place from which to embark on your charter. If you want to hit the beach, gen up first. On the southern coast are the cosmopolitan party beaches like Paradise and Super Paradise, which are busy day and night, whereas Órnos and Psaroú are great for families. To escape the crowds head along the northern coast to Ayia Ánna, Houlákia, Kápari, Agrári and Ayios Stéfanos.

Mykonos is renowned for its stylish boutiques and frenetic nightlife during the summer season. Often called the Ibiza of Greece, its party hot spots are teeming with beautiful people. Head to Chora and while away an afternoon shopping along glamorous Matoyánni Street, lined with brand name stores, charming cafés and stylish restaurants. In contrast, there are also many peaceful bays and anchorages as well as quiet rural villages. A must-do for every tourist is Little Venice, where medieval stone buildings were constructed right on the edge of the sea; their colourful wooden balconies overhang the water. The town has a romantic atmosphere, particularly at sunset. Order a cocktail in one of several welcoming restaurants and bars along the promenade.

destinations.name: Santorini
destinations.summary: The volcanic island of Santorini is widely considered to be one of the most beautiful and romantic in Europe. A yacht charter here makes the most of exploring all the sights and highlights on offer.
destinations.metaDescription: The volcanic island of Santorini is widely considered to be one of the most beautiful in Europe. Chartering a yacht here is an excellent choice.
destinations.lede: The volcanic island of Santorini is widely considered to be one of the most beautiful and romantic in Europe. A yacht charter here makes the most of exploring all the sights and highlights on offer.
paragraphs: Santorini’s landscape and seascape were formed by a volcanic explosion, which was allegedly the inspiration for the myth of Atlantis.

Today you can anchor off Kamari’s black pebble beach, visit the volcano and walk across the caldera. Head to Oia, balanced on a hilltop in the northwest, where whitewashed houses are built on gigantic rocks and woven by orange and lemon groves. The incredible sunsets here are beyond breath-taking; couples will be reminded of their first flush of romance.

destinations.name: Corfu
destinations.summary: Chartering a yacht in the beautiful cruising grounds of Corfu gives access to both north and south sides of the island, enabling visits to stunning vantage points that would otherwise be unreachable.
destinations.metaDescription: From pristine turquoise waters to colourful coastal housing, Corfu is a sight to behold. With the beauty lining the coast it is a perfect yacht charter destination.
destinations.lede: Chartering a yacht in delightful Corfu gives access to both north and south sides of the island, enabling visits to stunning vantage points that would otherwise be unreachable. North west of mainland Greece, Corfu is the second largest island in the Ionian Sea, just a short boat ride away from the Albanian coast.
paragraphs: An island immersed in Greek mythology. and in history, ravaged by a string of fearsome battles and violent conquests, Corfu today is astonishingly peaceful and pretty. Ticking all the boxes on a Mediterranean yacht charter checklist, visitors can enjoy the relaxed atmosphere, beautiful sunshine, cultural highlights and stunning landscapes. Where the northern part of the island is more mountainous and ringed by pebble beaches, the south is characterized by lush lowlands, wide, sandy beaches and tranquil bays.

Influenced by the English nobility, Greek education and Venetian style, Corfu attracts a cultured crowd. In the small capital Corfu city, the old town is a labyrinth of narrow, colourful cobblestone streets surrounded by vast fortifications. As a World Heritage Site, the architecture of the old town is well worth leaving the beaches for. While you’re on land, make a beeline to the lively locals haunt Tsipouradiko. Near the Old Port you can eat meze washed down with a lively glass of tsipouro.Those with a sweet tooth should stop at Papagiorgis, offering 40 different flavours of homemade ice cream. Enjoying a steady breeze all summer long, Corfu delivers culture, culinary flair and excellent sailing in the crystalline Ionian Sea – this is a great starting point from which to explore further.

destinations.name: Zakynthos
destinations.summary: An island blessed with fertile valleys dotted with olive groves and secluded coves fringed by sandy shores, sailing around the undulating coastline of Zakynthos is a real treat.
destinations.metaDescription: Zakynthos is an essential charter destination when cruising the Ionian. Ensure to visit Navagio Shipwreck Beach, famous for its azure waters and golden beach.
paragraphs: An island blessed with fertile valleys dotted with olive groves and secluded coves fringed by sandy shores, sailing around the undulating coastline of Zakynthos is a real treat. The harbour capital is a major hub, centered around busy Solomos Square. Popular beaches such as Agios Nikolaos, Alykanas and Tsilivi offer great opportunities to enjoy leisurely swimming and water sports.

With an abundance of pine tree strewn hills, the contrasting golden beaches are found in the north, east and south. In the west the rocky landscape has a number of sea caves including the famous Blue Grotto Caves. When the sun shines in the afternoon, it creates patterns in every blue hue imaginable across the cave walls.

Smugglers Cove is renowned for the large wreck nestling in a golden bay, the remains of a shipwreck in 1980, the story allegedly involves the black market and smuggling. Only accessed by yacht, this is a popular tourist attraction, but really has to be seen. Zakynthos (or Zante) Town, the islands’ capital, is a busy port with great shopping and restaurants. Sit with a chilled frappe and watch the world go by.

destinations.name: Hydra
destinations.summary: Approached from the water, Hydra is a beautiful hillside crescent of whitewashed houses, with the port nestling below. Meet the donkeys, visit stunning beaches and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere.
destinations.metaDescription: Approached from the water, Hydra is a beautiful hillside crescent of whitewashed houses with the port nestling below, perfectly suited for your yacht charter.
paragraphs: Approached from the water, Hydra is a beautiful hillside crescent of whitewashed houses, with the port nestling below. Meet the donkeys, visit stunning beaches and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Pretty much anywhere on the waterfront in Hydra will deliver a jaw-dropping view, but none more so than from the famous sunset lookout point which is a quick walk from the main port.

One of the most romantic destinations and often named the St Tropez of Greece, Hydra is home to a fabulously charismatic port. The arc-shaped harbour is lined with bustling boutiques, cool galleries and vibrant restaurants. The diverse mix of traditional waterfront mansions alongside the naval academy, backed by rows of stone houses displaying red rooftops alongside blue windows and doors is a vibrant blend. At each side of the harbour, cannons from days gone by face to sea and statues of the heroes of independence give a nod to history lessons. Hydra is the only town on the island; motorbikes and cars, even bicycles, are forbidden, and instead, transport is by donkey. Restored and preserved exactly as it appeared in the 1800’s; this is a listed architectural reserve, any new construction is (theoretically) banned, leaving this island adorably time-warped.

Dutifully eco-friendly and an atmospheric gem, Hydra is scattered with narrow cobbled streets rising steeply against lush foliage and craggy hills. Wander the elaborate backstreets for genuine Greek charm, radiating from tucked-away cafes, where resident felines wait for a titbit. Old-style tavernas are abundant, serving traditional dishes such as mouth-watering kydonato (veal and quinces) and delightful achladakia (almond pastries). Expect warm hospitality from the residents who gather along the harbour in the early evening, casually sipping espresso freddos and cold Mythos beers, they calmly indulge in the fascinating pastime of people-watching.

If you head away from the main town, the rest of the island is mountainous, barely inhabited and little visited, barring hilltop monasteries, goat farms and pine forests. However hikers enthuse that Hydra is paradise for adventure; so, if your walking boots need some action, this is the place. Despite not having sandy beaches, Hydra is not short of decent swimming spots. Recommended is pebbly Plakes beach with sparkling clear water and lunch at the Four Seasons taverna is delicious. The isolated beaches of Bisti Bay and Agios Nikolaos on the south western tip of Hydra are achingly gorgeous and often unoccupied. Best approached by yacht, drop anchor in this haven and spend dreamy hours lulled by the green waves lapping the pebbly shoreline, while local butterflies land helter skelter. Bariami Cave, near to the main town, is essentially a sea cave that is treated by locals like a swimming pool.

destinations.name: Spetses
destinations.summary: Rich in both history and beauty, Spetses is a serene island where horse and carriage is the preferred transport. Pine trees meet the sea at scenic coves and fish tavernas thrive at the old port.
destinations.metaDescription: Spetses is a serene island where horse and carriage is the preferred transport. Wander the cobbled streets and relax in the bay on your chartered yacht.
paragraphs: Rich in both history and beauty, Spetses in the Saronic Gulf is a wonderfully serene island, where horse and carriage is the preferred transport. Pine trees meet the sea at scenic coves and fish tavernas thrive at the old port.

Naturally enticing and ultimately charming, Spetses is an outstanding destination for visiting yachts. Rugged shores lapped by turquoise water beckon swimming and snorkelling to your heart’s content, while secluded anchorages are ideal for lunch on the aft deck.

Festivals are a big part of life on Spetses. In September, the impressive re-enactment of the famous local naval battle of the Greek revolution takes place. The “Armata” culminates in victory with the symbolic burning of an enemy flagship in the harbour, while fishing boats and sea-taxis hoist blue and red flags of the revolution emblazoned with the word “Spetses”. This is the most significant annual event in Spetses’ culture and lasts a whole week. At the start of September, the Festival of Agios Mamas occurs on a small beach near Dapia. Children gather at the foot of the church after evening mass and take small handmade boats filled with candles and sail them out to sea. This really is a beautiful and romantic sight.

Steeped in history and tradition, one of the most famous heroes of the Greek Revolution in Spetses was the female captain, Lascarina Bouboulina. Taking command of her murdered husband’s fleet, she was an active member of the Filiki Etairia, a secret organisation plotting the revolt. Also a great business woman, she paid over her fortune amassed from two husbands, to finance the war: indeed she built the famous ship Agamemnon, equipped with 18 cannons, the largest vessel used in the War of Independence. Many streets in Greece are named after her today as a mark of the esteem she is held in.
This enticing isle is a fascinating stopping point on a Saronic Islands yacht charter and a few days exploring is well worth the time.

destinations.name: Amalfi
destinations.summary: Set on dramatically cascading cliffs, the town of Amalfi is a cluster of vibrant buildings melded to the landscape. Scenic and peaceful, this yacht charter location is packed with true Italian charm.
destinations.metaDescription: Discover dramatically cascading cliffs that fold into a cluster of vibrant buildings from a unique angle on an Amalfi yacht charter.
paragraphs: Clusters of brightly painted buildings that meld into the cascading cliffside, Amalfi is a relaxed and scenic resort for a yacht charter, blessed with abundant Italian charm. Found between Salerno and Positano on the Italian coast, narrow alleyways wind up through the town between the sea and mountains. Folklore, traditions and indescribable beauty of the landscape: a luxury Amalfi yacht charter is without comparison.

Packed with history, Amalfi is the oldest of the four great maritime republics, taking advantage of military and trading power that delivered notoriety and architectural influence. Annual celebrations in the summer months see the spectacular June Regatta between republics battling for seafaring bragging rights.

The waterfront promenade skirts the marina filled with colourful boats, whilst the Piazza del Duomo in front of the impressive cathedral is the focal point of the historic centre, buzzing with cafes and boutiques in the square. Head up the 60 steps during an Amalfi luxury yacht charter and admire the Byzantine architecture and decoration of the Duomo di Sant’Andrea. With a long history of paper milling: stop at the Museo della Carta to view the attractive handmade products, indeed some family-owned mills still follow this tradition. In Amalfi, citrus scents fill the air thanks to the surrounding lemon groves laden with lemon trees. Enjoy some local limoncello liqueur and look out for pretty handmade ceramics decorated with fruit.

With some of the best beaches found along this coastline, Amalfi is blessed with crystal clear blue waters – great for swimming, snorkelling, diving and making use of your Amalfi yacht charter’s tenders and toys. The Emerald Grotto at Cape Conca is one of Amalfi’s great natural wonders, where sunlight refracts through an underwater crevice to emit an astonishing green hue.

destinations.name: Capri
destinations.summary: Unforgettable and magical, a Capri yacht charter is filled with Italian delights. From mouth-watering local dishes to panoramic views, this tiny isle in the Gulf of Naples packs a real punch.
destinations.metaDescription: Unforgettable, exclusive and magical, a Capri luxury yacht charter will bring boundless charm to any lavish Italian getaway. Start exploring.
paragraphs: Unforgettable, exclusive and magical, a Capri yacht charter is filled with Italian delights. From mouth-watering local dishes to panoramic views over crystalline waters, this tiny isle in the Gulf of Naples on the Italian coast packs a real punch.

On Italy’s most exclusive island and yacht charter destination, they say that finding a summer mooring for a yacht in Capri is like finding a diamond in the sand. But thanks to forward planning by your captain it will not be your concern! Near to Marina Piccola, drop anchor beyond the Faraglioni rocks. From the little tender dock take an old-school taxi with an iconic sunshade to properly explore the island. Cruise around the island on a typical Gozzo Classico but visit the Blue Grotto again later in privacy. Snorkelling and swimming here is unparalleled, as long as you beat the crowds, while the surrounding azure blue waters make it the ideal destination to make use of your luxury Capri yacht charter’s tenders and toys.

Ashore, don’t forgo the chance to wander around Villa San Michele, Axel Munthe’s fascinating mansion. At the Via Camarelle, it is credit cards at dawn, with international designers, bespoke shoemakers, sunglasses ateliers, artisan food shops and linen stores. There are a number of excellent gelaterias, selling mouth-watering ice cream – a must-try during a Capri yacht charter. Emperor Tiberio notably built 12 mansions on Capri and some of the ruins can still be visited today. First, get your bearings by walking up the steep path to Monte Solaro (almost 600m over sea level). Take an espresso at the top and soak up the spectacular panoramic views stretching out across the Bay of Naples and the Amalfi Coast, then catch the funicular back down. The island of Capri is a culinary paradise and exploring the island’s wonderful eateries and fine dining restaurants is a must during a Capri luxury yacht charter vacation. An aperitif on Piazzetta Capri makes for excellent people-watching, but go beyond the guidebook recommendations for incredible views at Ristorante Da Gelsomina in Anacapri.

destinations.name: Positano
destinations.summary: For those seeking unrivalled views, bustling restaurants and a vibrant lifestyle, a Positano yacht charter offers the simply sublime.
destinations.metaDescription: For those seeking unrivalled views, bustling restaurants and a vibrant lifestyle, a Positano yacht charter offers the simply sublime. Explore more here.
paragraphs: Bursting with life and boasting a small sandy beach coupled with exuding ambience, it is no wonder Positano is a popular yacht charter retreat. Approaching the dramatic bay of Positano by yacht is a truly magical experience. Known as the vertical town and surrounded by dramatic cliffs, Positano offers beautiful views, worth the many steps to enjoy them.

Many of the coves and picturesque bays surrounding this popular yachting destination are only accessible from the water. During a Positano yacht charter cruise to Fiordo di Furore for unique rock diving, the three Galli islands for stunning anchorages, or head to Fornillo where the beach is a peaceful haunt for discerning locals. After a day of exploration, relax on your Positano yacht charter with a handcrafted cocktail or enjoy an exquisite meal ashore.

For individuals in search of nightlife with an exclusive feel, don’t miss a visit to the hot spot ‘club-in-a-cave’ Music on the Rocks while on a yacht charter in Amalfi, regarded as one of the leading clubs in Europe.

destinations.name: Cinque Terre
destinations.summary: In Liguria, the five fishing towns of the Cinque Terre are a fascinating mix of perched and pastel-painted communities, surrounded by lush nature and best observed from your Cinque Terre Yacht Charter
destinations.metaTitle: Cinque Terre Yacht Charter: Five Ligurian Villages by Sea
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in the Cinque Terre and see all five UNESCO villages from the water, the way this coastline is best viewed. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: In Liguria, the five fishing towns of the Cinque Terre are a fascinating mix of perched and pastel-painted communities, surrounded by lush nature and best observed from your Cinque Terre Yacht Charter.
paragraphs: One of the lesser-known destinations to explore on Italy’s Ligurian coast is Cinque Terre. Many experienced captains will recommend cruising this idyllic stretch of coastline to their charter clients and owners, as it is largely inaccessible except by boat or train. Directly translated, Cinque Terre means ‘Five Lands’; namely the coastal villages of Monterosso al Mare, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola, and Riomaggiore. This unique region is part of the Cinque Terre National Park and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

Here, hilltop houses are painted in a range of vivid colours so that local fishermen can see their homes from the sea. No big label shops will take your attention from the main event: lunch. Meander through the narrow streets, stop and sip an ice-cold limoncello and soak up the laid back atmosphere with a plate of fresh antipasti. Here’s a place to slow down and watch the world go by on your Cinque Terre luxury yacht charter. Make a beeline for Ristorante Minky where you will struggle to choose between an array of daily specials in lashings of lemon butter, garlic and herbs. Hike the Sentiero Azzurro trail connecting the villages along a cliff top path. Finally, cycle through the vineyards and swim from the aft deck to see abundant marine life.

destinations.name: Genoa
destinations.summary: Often nicknamed La Superba, and once one of the great city states of Italy, Genoa has a proud maritime history making it a compelling destination for yachting enthusiasts.
destinations.metaTitle: Genoa Yacht Charter: Ligurian Capital and Riviera Coast
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Genoa and cruise Liguria from its historic port, with Portofino and the Cinque Terre within easy reach. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: Often nicknamed La Superba, and once one of the great city states of Italy, Genoa has a proud maritime history making it a compelling destination for yachting enthusiasts passing through the western Mediterranean. Admire the city that stands on a hillside above the splendid harbour from your Genoa yacht charter.
paragraphs: As a cultural capital it benefits from numerous museums, some housed in palaces, and also hosts several cultural events. Be sure to make time during your Genoa luxury yacht charter to visit the maritime museum and the giant aquarium, the largest in Europe.
Genoa was the birthplace of Christopher Columbus, and history lovers will appreciate a tour of the old harbour, Port Antico, which was restored to its former glory in 2004.

For more earthly pleasures while on a Genoa luxury yacht charter, the city boasts plenty of chic boutiques and a sophisticated bar and restaurant scene. The town is typically Italian in its design: lavish arcades and leafy piazzas, populated with fine shops and convivial pavement cafés in which you can while away the heat of the afternoon. Plan your Genoa yacht charter for a perfect pairing of history and modernity, tradition and innovation, all set against a picture-perfect Italian landscape.

destinations.name: Lerici
destinations.summary: At the eastern end of the Italian Riviera, on the bay of La Spezia, the idyllic Ligurian township of Lerici is well known for its secluded beaches and dramatic mountains diving straight into the sea.
destinations.metaDescription: For those seeking an extraordinary yacht charter in La Spezia, prepare to be amazed by the secluded beaches and dramatic mountains that plunge into the sea.
destinations.lede: Lerici is a Ligurian township at the eastern end of the Italian Riviera and the ideal location for a yacht charter in La Spezia. The idyllic seaside town on the bay of La Spezia is well known for its fabulous secluded beaches and dramatic mountains that plunge straight into the sea.
paragraphs: The relative privacy of La Spezia has, over the years, drawn a crowd of philosophers, writers, and poets, from Dante to Shelley and Byron, earning it the nickname Golfo dei Poeti, the Bay of Poets.
The landscape certainly inspires creativity, from the waterfront piazza with its trompe-l’oeil frescoed buildings to the charming seaside cafés lining the harbour.

Yachts and gozzi, the typical small fishing boats of the area, jostle for space. The medieval fishing village is dominated by the castle. Built during the 11th century on a rocky promontory, it towers above the port.

Head along Via Roma during a yacht charter in La Spezia, where you can dip into the many boutiques selling traditional Italian goods and high fashion. The Gothic chapel Sant Anastasio at the top of the castle offers stunning views across the Riviera and the Golfo dei Poeti. If you are travelling with children, a morning spent at the Castello di Lerici’s Museo Geopaleontologico will enthral little ones, who will marvel at life-size dinosaurs and can experience a simulated earthquake.
Lerici is the ideal location for an Italian Riviera yacht charter where you can enjoy natural beauty, culture, and gastronomy at its finest.

destinations.name: Portofino
destinations.summary: Exquisite and stylish - a luxury yacht charter haven - if there is one place that deserves the mantle of Italy’s most exclusive resort, it has to be Portofino.
destinations.metaTitle: Portofino Yacht Charter: Ligurian Harbour and Coastline
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Portofino and anchor in its pastel harbour, with Santa Margherita and the abbey of San Fruttuoso nearby. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: If there is one place that deserves the mantle of Italy’s most exclusive resort, it has to be Portofino. Not because of the stellar crowd who have graced its pretty promenades since the days of the Grand Tour, but because of its ability to be at the forefront of the social scene and yet retain an air of casual, mellow dolce far niente, making a Portofino yacht charter a beautiful experience.
paragraphs: Portofino is a foodie’s dream, with its abundance of top-notch eateries providing authentic Italian dishes, fresh seafood and homemade pasta. On your yacht charter in Portofino, make sure to stop at any of these top eateries:

If you’re a seafood fan, you can’t miss Restaurant Puny, right in the middle of Portofino. Spaghetti with mussels, grilled octopus, and sea bass fillet are just a few of the excellent seafood dishes available. The restaurant’s beautiful setting and extensive wine and beverage list make it ideal for a special date.

La Terrazza is a trendy and sophisticated restaurant with a wide selection of Italian and international specialties, perched on a hill overlooking the harbor. Risotto, tagliatelle with truffles, and veal Milanese are just a few of the traditional Italian meals available, along with seafood and vegetarian alternatives. The wine list is also top-notch, with several selections hailing from Piedmont.

Da I Gemelli is a lovely family-run trattoria with a nice indoor dining area and a lovely outdoor patio, perfect for a more relaxed meal. Homemade ravioli, grilled meats, and authentic Ligurian pesto are just a few examples of the menu’s modest yet wonderful offerings. The local wines at this restaurant are excellent, and the service is warm and pleasant.
Portofino is known for its excellent dining options, but that’s not all it has to offer. On your yacht charter in Portofino, don’t miss out on these top attractions:

Castello Brown, a historic castle, sits atop a hill with breathtaking views of Portofino and the bay below. The castle, which dates back to the 16th century but has recently undergone restoration, is now a museum. The castle’s rooms house a variety of displays for guests to peruse and enjoy.

San Fruttuoso Abbey is a stunning monastery from the 10th century that sits in a hidden bay between Portofino and Camogli and can only be reached by boat or on foot. There is a beautiful nature reserve all around the abbey, and guests can also explore the monastery’s cathedral and crypt. In addition, the area is home to a number of scenic hiking paths that provide stunning panoramas of the ocean.

Santa Margherita Ligure is a picturesque coastal town located just a short drive from Portofino. The town is known for its lovely promenade, colorful buildings, and active marina. The town’s famous focaccia bread can be sampled while taking a stroll along the waterfront. There are also several great seafood eateries serving up the day’s catch and other regional delicacies.

If you have any energy remaining after visiting the cultural attractions and indulging in the endless options for food and drink, there are plenty of options to get active and explore some more of Portofino.

Snorkeling and scuba diving are excellent in the pristine waters around Portofino. Punta del Capo and San Fruttuoso Marine Park are just two of the many fantastic diving locations in the region; while there, you might spot dolphins, octopuses, and a rainbow of tropical species. You can snorkel or dive at your own pace thanks to the snorkeling and diving gear provided by many boat charters.

Sailing and boating enthusiasts flock to Portofino for the numerous opportunities to explore the shore. Portofino is a great place to rent a sailboat or motorboat and cruise around the many bays and inlets in the area, or to go on a guided trip with a local. Kayaks, paddleboards, and jet skis are just some of the water sports equipment that accompany most yacht charters in Portofino.

There are several trails and hills in the Portofino area that are perfect for hikers and trekkers who want to see the area’s stunning scenery up close. The Way of the Gods and Monte di Portofino Natural Park are just two of the many hiking routes that lead to breathtaking vistas and private beaches. You can go on a guided hiking tour with a yacht charter, or you can go off and discover on your own with a good map and sturdy hiking boots.

destinations.name: Pontine Islands
destinations.summary: The Pontine Islands offer charming Italian atmosphere together with a wealth of snorkelling/diving sites. Lesser known and filled with history, this pretty archipelago offers a true yachting getaway.
destinations.metaDescription: For those seeking a unique yacht charter, Pontine Islands offer charming Italian atmosphere together with a wealth of snorkelling/diving sites.
destinations.lede: Six islands in total make up the pretty Pontine archipelago, with alluring Ventotene and Ponza the largest and best known. For tranquillity and sheer charm, these islands are a wonderful destination for relaxed cruising, exploring ashore and some excellent underwater discoveries.
paragraphs: Clandestine and inviting, the rugged island of Ponza is a quaint yachting haven where windless coves dot the coastline. Casual restaurants deliver understated nightlife with sunset aperitifs and delicious fresh fare; this is a place to relish unmitigated Italian charm with laid-back simplicity.

Without any permanent inhabitants or a port, the diminutive islet of Gavi nearby attracts few visitors, but the shallow waters close to its shore provide superb swimming and snorkelling. Look out for the Grottone di Gavi in the rocky outcrops.

Ventotene is perfect for water lovers, with opportunities to explore an underwater world full of shipwrecks and marine life. A true getaway isle to soak up the vibe and relax amongst the beautiful scenery or head ashore to stroll the ancient Via Olivi. The sandy stretch at Cala Nave is a great anchorage to enjoy the clear waters.

Picturesque and inviting, the rocky islet of Palmarola is the pearl of the Pontines, with crystalline waters and secret caves. This protected nature reserve is also a diver’s paradise, claimed by Jacques Cousteau to be the most beautiful island in the Mediterranean.

Tiny Santo Stefano measures just 400 metres from one side to the other. Once a penal colony, it is now completely uninhabited. The main sight here is the abandoned prison which can be visited by a guided excursion. The mix of azure waters around the island are quite extraordinary and home to rich marine life.

Craggy Zannone has a somewhat chequered past, made famous by a group of adventurous aristocrats. However these days, the island’s only inhabitants left are a flock of mouflon wild sheep, brought specifically to the island to liven up hunting. Raw nature and wild allure give this isle its blissful appeal.

destinations.name: Olbia
destinations.summary: Olbia is a port city on the northeast coast of Sardinia, Italy. It is one of the most popular destinations in Italy for luxury yacht charters.
destinations.metaTitle: Olbia Yacht Charter: Gateway to the Costa Smeralda Coast
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in Olbia and cruise the Costa Smeralda, the Maddalena archipelago and the granite coastline of Sardinia. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: Olbia is a port city on the northeast coast of Sardinia, Italy. It is one of the most popular destinations in Italy for luxury yacht charters. Olbia has a wide variety of things to do and is perfect for those who are looking to explore Corsica, the Mediterranean, or even enjoy a luxurious motor yacht experience.
paragraphs: Acting as the northwestern gateway to the emerald coast of Sardinia, we explore what to do in Olbia and our favourite places to visit. The ancient city of Olbia welcomes visitors with a palm-strewn waterfront, bustling cafe culture and highly sought-after beaches. World famous celebs flock here for boutique shopping, delicious restaurants and fun nightlife.

Winding lanes leading from Corso Umberto reveal unassuming, family-run restaurants to enjoy delicious traditional food and local wines as you watch the world go by; indeed the charm of Olbia undoubtedly lies in its laidback piazza’s and the ritual evening passeggiata. Visit the superb archaeological museum, set on its own little fortified island, to discover the full story of early Greek settlers and the subsequent rich history of Olbia, then wander the back streets and find the Pisan-style basilica of San Simplicio which is well worth a visit.

The sheltered bay of Costa Corallina provides great anchorage for luxury yacht charters in Olbia, opposite the quiet stretch beach with crystalline, shallow waters: this is a top spot for kayaking and snorkelling. Alternatively, for some good windsurfing grounds, make for the long stretch of reddish sands on Spiaggia della Saline, lying between the sea and salt flats, populated by elegant flamingos.

destinations.name: The Aeolian Islands
destinations.summary: Peppering the Tyrrhenian Sea just off Sicily's northeast coast, the Aeolians are a group of seven UNESCO protected islands with volcanic origins and varied landscapes.
destinations.metaTitle: Aeolian Islands Yacht Charter: Stromboli and Volcanoes
destinations.metaDescription: Charter a crewed yacht in the Aeolian Islands and cruise this UNESCO archipelago off Sicily, from the eruptions of Stromboli to Panarea. Enquire today.
destinations.lede: Peppering the Tyrrhenian Sea just off Sicily's northeast coast, the Aeolians are a group of seven UNESCO protected islands with volcanic origins and varied landscapes.
paragraphs: The main island, Lipari, has a vibrant town and is a great place from which to explore. Visit Vulcano, famed for its vast and sweeping black sand beaches and mud baths. Remote Stromboli, dominated by the active volcano Gran Cratere, offers incredible views for adventurous hikers and regular magma firework displays at night.

Those who prefer a gentle walk can drop anchor off Salina, a lush, hilly island, crammed with history. Don’t miss Pollara – a beautiful bay with an underwater crater. Panarea is the smallest and most refined island. With an upmarket shopping street and a number of quaint hotels dotted between huge, private villas in lush gardens, this is a culinary haven with a surprisingly busy nightlife. For ultimate escapism, head west to the smallest islands, Filicudi and Alicudi; catch your own fish, BBQ on deck and wash them down with some Sicilian wine. On the uninhabited west coast of Alicudi, the seclusion of sheer rock walls make for a great swimming spot in total privacy.

destinations.name: Formentera
destinations.summary: Nicknamed ‘Little Caribbean’, and considered by many to be the most beautiful of the Balearics, Formentera is a paradise for sun worshippers.
destinations.metaDescription: Nicknamed ‘Little Caribbean’, and considered by many to be the most beautiful of the Balearics, Formentera is a paradise for sun worshippers.
destinations.lede: Nicknamed ‘Little Caribbean’, and considered by many to be the most beautiful of the Balearics, Formentera is a paradise for sun worshippers.
paragraphs: Formentera is the southernmost Balearic Island lying nine nautical miles south of Ibiza. But while Ibiza basks in the limelight of its own celebrity, quieter, calmer Formentera has no airport and can only be reached by boat.

Many of the island’s pristine beaches are deserted, even in high summer. Es Palmador is an uninhabited island, only accessible by boat to the north of Formentera: connected by ‘Es Pas’ sand bar: it’s possible to walk waist deep from one island to the other – just don’t run aground.
